EVENTS.adm: Balisan, north-east of Erbil (Erbil province, KRI)
EVENTS.h: Missile fired at Iranian Kurdish opposition camp north-east of Erbil
EVENTS.s: A missile was fired at an Iranian Kurdish opposition camp north-east of Iraq's Erbil on 21 October, security sources told Reuters. Kurdish media quoted a spokesman for the Kurdistan Freedom Party (PAK) as saying two to four projectiles struck its positions near Hasanawa village in the Balisan mountains at about 09:30 with no casualties, and a security source said Iran was believed to have used two drones. It is the fourth reported Iranian strike on opposition camps in Erbil province this month, after drones hit a Khabat district site on 8 October, the PDKI's Azadi camp near Koya on 12 October and a Komala base in Balisan on 17 October, none of which caused reported casualties.
EVENTS.impl: Restricted · essential travel with advance, Erbil under drone threat. The Kurdistan Region remains the most active theatre: Iranian drone and missile strikes on Iranian-Kurdish opposition camps in Erbil province were reported on 8, 12, 17 and 21 October (Reuters confirmed the 21 October missile strike north-east of Erbil), none causing reported casualties but all unanswered since coalition air defences left with the 30 September US withdrawal, and on 20 October Tehran's ambassador claimed Baghdad had agreed to expel or hand over the groups, a claim Iraqi officials have not confirmed and the KDPI rejects.

EVENTS.h: Putin meets Witkoff in St Petersburg, frees jailed American, floats Trump summit in China
EVENTS.s: President Putin received US envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg on 21 October, a day after Witkoff's Oslo talks with Zelensky, and proposed meeting President Trump in China; Witkoff said there was a basis for a ceasefire and urged Putin to consider resuming three-way US-Russia-Ukraine talks. Putin announced that Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired US teacher held since 2022 on mercenary charges, had been freed and taken to Pulkovo airport. Witkoff travelled without Jared Kushner, who was ill.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active deep-strike campaign and arbitrary detention. Russia's two principal cities remain under sustained Ukrainian drone attack: the 18 October assault on St Petersburg was the largest yet, killing one, injuring 15 and setting the city's oil terminal ablaze, while Reuters reported a 15 October strike that set fire to the Ryazan refinery feeding Moscow and Russian media reported repeated closures of all four Moscow airports through mid-October.

EVENTS.h: Night curfews extended in Paris and other cities; troops to back police for 24 October protests
EVENTS.s: After targeted curfews from the night of 19 October around Place de la République and Les Halles in Paris, part of Lyon's Presqu'île and for minors in Lille, Douai, Wattignies, Denain and central Nice produced a calm night, police extended them for Tuesday night and Marseille added a minors' curfew around commercial areas hit by looting. PM Sébastien Lecornu told parliament on 20 October that the deployment for the next protest day on Saturday 24 October 'will be massive', with Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez confirming military personnel would be deployed alongside police in static guard roles; both admitted intelligence failures, over-static deployments and the error of not cancelling police leave, and Nuñez apologised. Parliament is setting up a commission of inquiry, 200 investigators are tracking rioters, and a man on a security watch list belonging to an ultra-left group was arrested on 20 October over the Limoges town hall fire.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · curfew-aware movement planning. France is the epicentre of the European unrest wave: a month-old student movement fused with cost-of-living anger on 17 October into nationwide rioting that left 997 police injured, 2,397 arrested and at least 3,000 shops looted, prompting the first big-city curfews in years, which were extended on 20 October and are to remain 'as long as necessary'.

EVENTS.adm: Arlit–Agadez road, c. 35 km from Agadez, Agadez region
EVENTS.h: Gunmen ambush two escorted passenger buses near Agadez, killing at least 11
EVENTS.s: Gunmen aboard three vehicles attacked two passenger buses that had left the uranium-mining town of Arlit on the morning of Tuesday 20 October, killing at least 11 people and wounding several just outside Agadez, local broadcaster Tegades TV reported and an Agadez resident confirmed to AFP. A wounded passenger said the convoy 'ran into bandits who opened fire on us' and that soldiers escorting the buses exchanged fire with the attackers. Nigerien authorities had not commented and no group had claimed the attack; local outlet Journal du Niger reported ten passengers and one soldier killed and said one vehicle was reportedly carrying a large quantity of gold, suggesting a targeted robbery (unconfirmed). Northern Niger has largely been spared jihadist violence but is a trafficking corridor and home to anti-junta armed groups and gold-mining-related violence.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · essential travel only with state-level clearance. The first confirmed mass-casualty attack of the window struck the north rather than the jihadist-hit west: gunmen ambushed two escorted passenger buses on the Arlit–Agadez road on 20 October, killing at least 11 (AFP), on the only road corridor used by mining and humanitarian traffic between Agadez and the uranium belt; whether bandits, gold-robbers or anti-junta rebels, the escort failed to prevent it.

EVENTS.h: Kenya confirms ninth Ebola case; all linked to index patient, no community spread
EVENTS.s: Kenya's Health Ministry said on 20 October that a 24-year-old man, a close relative of the first patient who was already in quarantine, tested positive for Bundibugyo Ebola on 19 October, bringing the country's total to nine cases including one death. Director-General Patrick Amoth said eight patients were stable and responding to treatment and 134 of 135 identified contacts had been traced and quarantined; the ministry has imposed no restrictions on travel, trade or public gatherings. The index case, who arrived from the DRC via Uganda, died in Nairobi on 5 October; the DRC outbreak has exceeded 9,000 cases and 4,000 deaths since May and the Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccine.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · health screening. Nairobi and the main business corridors are operating normally, but the risk picture has shifted in two weeks: an imported Bundibugyo Ebola case has produced a nine-case cluster of relatives and healthcare workers in the capital, with no community transmission reported and 134 of 135 contacts quarantined, and the US has moved Kenya to Level 3 while explicitly flagging kidnapping and carjacking.

EVENTS.h: Two men rearrested under National Security Act for assisting Iranian intelligence over air base plot
EVENTS.s: Counter Terrorism Policing rearrested a 24-year-old British national, first detained outside RAF Fairford on 27 September, and a 25-year-old British-Iranian dual national, first detained in Westminster on 1 October, under section 3 of the National Security Act 2023 on suspicion of assisting a foreign intelligence service; police said the country concerned is Iran. Seven men have been arrested in total and all had been on bail; no one has been charged. Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor said it remains highly likely there was Iranian state involvement. US B-1 bombers that had used Fairford for strikes on Iran were withdrawn shortly after the September arrests.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · elevated state-threat activity. The UK's security picture is dominated by Iranian state-linked activity: the Fairford investigation moved on 20 October to National Security Act rearrests for assisting Iranian intelligence, a separate intrusion at RAF Molesworth is being handled under the same act, and MI5 warned on 13 October that Iran and Russia are stepping up hybrid campaigns.

EVENTS.h: Trucker blockades leave supermarket shelves and fuel pumps empty in southern Italy
EVENTS.s: A week-long protest by truck drivers against diesel prices roughly a third higher than before the Iran war blocked loading and unloading at supermarket distribution warehouses near Naples on 19 October, leaving some supermarket shelves and petrol pumps empty in the city on 20 October, with shortages of fresh pasta, cheese, meat and produce reported in Sicily, Calabria and Apulia, partly due to stockpiling. Roadblocks continued on the A2 and A30 in Campania and Calabrian hauliers announced a strike until 27 October, while restrictions in Sicily were lifted. Transport Minister Matteo Salvini met trucking associations on 20 October and promised tax credits to offset diesel costs.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · avoid city-centre protest zones. Italy has moved from routine strike disruption to sustained violent unrest: the 17-18 October riots in Milan, with clashes in Turin, Bologna, Brescia and Bergamo, injured more than 100 police, and the government responded on 20 October with 500 extra soldiers for Milan and an emergency decree creating new protest offences, while luxury retailers in the centre boarded up.

EVENTS.h: Iran says Iraq agreed to expel or hand over Iranian Kurdish opposition groups; Baghdad silent
EVENTS.s: Iran's ambassador to Iraq, Mohammad Kazem Al-Sadegh, said on 20 October that during a meeting of the Iraq-Iran joint security commission attended by Iraq's National Security Adviser the two sides agreed to expel members of 'Iranian separatist terrorist groups' from the Kurdistan Region or hand them over to Iran. The announcement came after senior Iraqi security officials had repeatedly told AFP that Baghdad was refusing to do so, fearing for the exiles' lives; the Iraqi statement on the 19 October meeting, which a Kurdistan Regional Government delegation also attended, mentioned only 'current challenges'. Under a 2023 agreement Iraq disarmed the groups and moved them to camps away from the border, but Iran has resumed deadly attacks on them since the Middle East war began in late February; the KDPI said it would not lay down its weapons.
EVENTS.impl: Restricted · essential travel with advance, Erbil under drone threat. The Kurdistan Region remains the most active theatre: Iranian drone and missile strikes on Iranian-Kurdish opposition camps in Erbil province were reported on 8, 12, 17 and 21 October (Reuters confirmed the 21 October missile strike north-east of Erbil), none causing reported casualties but all unanswered since coalition air defences left with the 30 September US withdrawal, and on 20 October Tehran's ambassador claimed Baghdad had agreed to expel or hand over the groups, a claim Iraqi officials have not confirmed and the KDPI rejects.

EVENTS.h: Nigeria confirms first Ebola case in a decade in Abuja; 44 contacts traced
EVENTS.s: Nigeria confirmed Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) in a woman who arrived in Abuja via Addis Ababa on 5 October, fell ill two days later and was admitted to a private hospital on 11 October with malaria-like symptoms; the positive result was confirmed on Tuesday 20 October, Reuters reported. Authorities have identified 44 contacts, most of them healthcare workers, and are tracing fellow passengers. Nigeria is the fourth African country hit by the outbreak, which has killed 4,646 people since May and has no approved treatment or vaccine; Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate said the patient is in isolation and that the country contained Ebola in 2014.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · North-east, Zamfara and Kaduna corridor no-go · Abuja medical watch. The north-east remains in its most dangerous phase in years: Boko Haram/ISWAP overran the Guzamala base on 13 October (at least 10 soldiers killed per Reuters) and killed 10 soldiers and five CJTF in a mine-and-ambush attack on a patrol near Gamboru Ngala on 17 October, despite military claims of more than 100 militants killed in airstrikes.

EVENTS.h: Slovakia to resume intergovernmental talks with Russia on 26 October in new break with EU allies
EVENTS.s: The Slovak Foreign Ministry said late on 20 October that the Russian-Slovak intergovernmental commission for economic, scientific and technical cooperation will meet in Moscow on 26 October, its first session since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, focusing on energy including gas and oil supplies, nuclear power, farming and culture. The move follows repeated Moscow visits by PM Robert Fico, who has criticised EU sanctions and halted military aid to Ukraine, and comes as parliament on 14 October narrowly approved a 2027 election-year budget widening the deficit to 4.94% of GDP. No protests or security incidents were reported in the window.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · routine. No terrorism, sabotage, violent protest or transport disruption was confirmed in Slovakia between 7 and 21 October.

EVENTS.h: Zelensky, Witkoff, Store and Stubb hold Ukraine talks in Oslo under heavy security
EVENTS.s: President Zelensky met US envoy Steve Witkoff, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store and Finnish President Alexander Stubb in Oslo on 20 October, with Jared Kushner joining remotely because of illness; Zelensky also brought intelligence chief Rustem Umerov and lawmaker Davyd Arakhamia. A US official called the talks 'constructive' and Witkoff flew on to St Petersburg to meet Putin on 21 October. The summit at the Grand Hotel passed without reported protest or incident.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · heightened hybrid vigilance. Norway remains a low-risk operating environment; the only in-window event affecting movement was the security operation around the 20 October Oslo talks between Zelensky, Witkoff, Store and Stubb, which passed without incident.

EVENTS.h: East-based parliament approves 2019 Türkiye maritime deal, lifts 2020 boycott; Greece objects
EVENTS.s: On Tuesday 20 October the east-based House of Representatives unanimously approved the 2019 Türkiye–GNA maritime boundaries memorandum and revoked two 2020 resolutions that had rejected the Turkish memorandums and cut political relations with Ankara, lawmakers Tarek al-Jeroushi and Aisha al-Tabalqi told Reuters; Greece swiftly rejected the decision as without legal effect and a violation of the law of the sea. The vote came two weeks after the chamber elected Salaheen Abdul Nabi as speaker on 6 October, ending Aguila Saleh's 12-year tenure (UNSMIL statement, 8 Oct). The move signals a rare east–west convergence around Ankara, which has long backed the Tripoli-based government, while raising friction with Greece, Cyprus and Egypt.
EVENTS.impl: No-go for routine travel · essential only with armed escort and air evacuation plan. Libya remains Critical: the 18 October Zawiya mortar blast (at least nine security personnel dead, Reuters) shows how militia and security-force camps embedded in populated areas generate casualties even without active fighting, while UNSMIL's 9 October statement on enforced disappearances in Tripoli and Ghat confirms the kidnap and arbitrary-detention threat to foreigners.

EVENTS.h: Drones hit Nyala and Khartoum; 17 killed in South Darfur, four in capital
EVENTS.s: An early-morning drone attack on Nyala, the RSF-held capital of South Darfur, struck the city centre and destroyed two homes, killing 17 people including seven RSF officers and wounding 23, medical and RSF sources told AFP. The same morning a drone hit a house east of Khartoum airport, killing four including three children aged two to six, while an army official said air defences intercepted RSF drones targeting the airport; a military source said RSF drones aimed at the Atbara and Setit dams were also shot down. The UN said the Khartoum attacks forced the cancellation of several flights, and medics and rights groups put the toll from drone strikes across Sudan in recent days above 160.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active conflict. The war is in a drone-dominated phase in which both SAF and RSF strike markets, funerals, displacement camps, dams, power plants and airports far behind the front lines: the 18-19 October wave in West Kordofan, Nyala and Khartoum killed well over 100 by AFP's count, the army's 19 October strike on Abyei's Amiet market (at least 153 dead per local officials) shows it will hit RSF supply lines across the South Sudan border, and the UN reported a 20 October drone strike on the Tendelti power station in White Nile.

EVENTS.h: Sudanese drone strike on Abyei's Amiet market kills at least 153
EVENTS.s: A drone strike on Amiet Market, about 10 km north of Abyei town, hit a nearby fuel depot at about 11:00 on 19 October, igniting a fire that was still burning the next day; Abyei's caretaker information minister Yohanna Akol Ngor told AP 153 deaths had been recorded and the toll was still rising, after Reuters had earlier reported 73 killed and 19 wounded. A senior Sudanese military officer told AP the army struck fuel tankers bound for the RSF and that the dead were RSF members and smugglers, which AP could not verify. The UN secretary-general condemned the attacks near Amiet and Todach, UNISFA was verifying casualties with many still missing, MSF treated more than 20 wounded at Ameth Bek Hospital, and South Sudan summoned Sudan's ambassador in protest.
EVENTS.impl: No-go outside Juba · essential travel only. South Sudan is now absorbing direct spillover from Sudan's drone war: the 19 October Amiet market strike in Abyei, which a Sudanese officer told AP targeted RSF-bound fuel tankers, is the deadliest single incident in the country this year and signals that supply corridors through South Sudanese territory will be targeted again; Juba has summoned Sudan's ambassador but has no means to deter further strikes.

EVENTS.adm: Valencia and Alicante provinces, Catalonia, Balearic Islands
EVENTS.h: Storm Adam floods eastern Spain: at least four dead, more than 2,000 evacuated
EVENTS.s: Storm Adam brought exceptional rain to Spain's Mediterranean coast from 17 October, peaking on 19 October when Pego (Alicante) recorded 632 mm in 36 hours. At least four people died: a 79-year-old woman found in her flooded home and a 64-year-old man who suffered a heart attack at a campsite in Oliva, a woman found on a beach at Sagunto and a woman swept into a stream at Cabrera de Mar near Barcelona; Spanish media reported a fifth body, an elderly man, found in the Pego-Oliva marsh on 20 October. Helicopters winched residents from rooftops, more than 2,000 people were evacuated mainly in Oliva, about 800,000 residents of 145 municipalities were under shelter-in-place orders on Monday morning, roads including the AP-7 were cut and Ibiza airport closed twice. Alerts were downgraded on 20 October and PM Pedro Sánchez visited Oliva.
EVENTS.src: Al Jazeera with AFP and Reuters, 20 Oct 2026
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · weather recovery and protest watch. Spain's immediate risk is environmental: Storm Adam killed at least four people in the Valencia region and Catalonia, alerts were lifted on 20 October and clean-up in Oliva, Pego and the Marina Alta will disrupt road travel for days, with orange warnings lingering in the Balearics.

EVENTS.adm: Nationwide (Ségou, Mopti/Bandiagara, Kidal and Gao regions)
EVENTS.h: HRW: Malian army and Africa Corps drone strikes killed 94 civilians April–August
EVENTS.s: Human Rights Watch said in a report on Monday 19 October that Mali's armed forces and their Russian Africa Corps backers carried out 'apparent indiscriminate' drone strikes and other abuses during a ramped-up offensive after the 25 April insurgent attacks that killed the defence minister. The report said 47 drone strikes killed 94 civilians between April and August, up from 22 strikes and 44 deaths a year earlier, including a 19 August strike on a cattle market in Bandiagara that killed six men and a 29 July pre-dawn strike on a health centre in Kidal region; it also documented soldiers shooting dead five girls mistaken for attackers in Ségou on 12 July, and the torture and execution of at least 19 captured soldiers by JNIM and FLA fighters near Tabrichat, Gao region, on 18 July. A Malian army spokesperson did not respond and Mali has previously denied killing civilians, Reuters reported.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active conflict. Mali is in open, multi-front war: JNIM has held the Bamako approaches under a renewed fuel blockade since late April and inflicted the heaviest losses on the army in years in September, while ISSP's killing of at least 48 civilians (local tolls 50–70+) in Daoussahak camps around Tagadayat, Ménaka, on 18–19 October, described by Reuters' sources as reprisal for killings of suspected informants by the MSA militia and Africa Corps, shows the IS affiliate escalating in the east and the cycle of atrocity and counter-atrocity tightening, even as ISSP and JNIM fight each other across the Burkina border.

EVENTS.h: Queimados municipal secretary shot dead by police on Avenida Brasil
EVENTS.s: On the night of Monday 19 October Jefferson Dias da Silva, 51, municipal secretary for economic development of Queimados (Baixada Fluminense) and a former councillor, was shot dead when Military Police officers of the 22nd Battalion (Maré) fired on his car. The Military Police said officers 'tried to stop a vehicle on Avenida Brasil, westbound, near Bonsucesso' and that the circumstances will be clarified by the ongoing investigation; witnesses told local media the car had ignored a stop order and two lanes of the expressway were closed. Acting Governor Ricardo Couto ordered the officers involved removed from duty and the PM command opened an internal inquiry; the Capital Homicide Division has taken statements and is analysing body-camera footage.
EVENTS.src: Agência Brasil (federal public news agency, carrying Military Police, Civil Police and Rio state government statements), 20 Oct 2026
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · Rio metro elevated through 25-26 Oct; avoid favela-adjacent routes, Avenida Brasil at night and election-day crowds. Brazil is four days from a polarised presidential runoff (Flávio Bolsonaro 47% vs Lula 45% in the 4 October first round; a bitter first debate on 18 October, per Reuters) in which public security is the dominant issue.

EVENTS.h: US raises Kenya travel advisory to Level 3 over Ebola, crime, terrorism
EVENTS.s: The US State Department raised Kenya from Level 2 to Level 3 'Reconsider Travel' on 19 October, citing health risk after the CDC issued a travel health notice for Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease, plus crime, kidnapping, terrorism, unrest and traffic safety. Eastleigh and Kibera in Nairobi, Garissa, Wajir, Mandera, Lamu and Tana River counties and coastal areas north of Malindi remain Level 4 'Do Not Travel', and Marsabit and Turkana within 50 km of the Ethiopian border are flagged over unrest. The advisory tells US citizens to avoid demonstrations and crowds and keep a low profile.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · health screening. Nairobi and the main business corridors are operating normally, but the risk picture has shifted in two weeks: an imported Bundibugyo Ebola case has produced a nine-case cluster of relatives and healthcare workers in the capital, with no community transmission reported and 134 of 135 contacts quarantined, and the US has moved Kenya to Level 3 while explicitly flagging kidnapping and carjacking.

EVENTS.h: Largest-ever drone attack on St Petersburg kills one, injures 15, sets oil terminal ablaze
EVENTS.s: One person was killed and 15 injured in a Ukrainian drone attack on oil facilities, logistics and data centres in St Petersburg and the Leningrad region overnight on 18 October, local authorities said. Governor Alexander Beglov said fires broke out at the St Petersburg oil terminal, an oil depot and industrial warehouses; Ozon said its logistics hub was on fire and VK said its Leningrad-region data centre was hit. Russia's Defence Ministry said air defences downed 1,015 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions overnight, one of the largest bombardments of the war.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active deep-strike campaign and arbitrary detention. Russia's two principal cities remain under sustained Ukrainian drone attack: the 18 October assault on St Petersburg was the largest yet, killing one, injuring 15 and setting the city's oil terminal ablaze, while Reuters reported a 15 October strike that set fire to the Ryazan refinery feeding Moscow and Russian media reported repeated closures of all four Moscow airports through mid-October.

EVENTS.adm: Tagadayat / Tinabow area, c. 50 km from Ménaka town, Ménaka region
EVENTS.h: ISSP kills at least 48 civilians in Ménaka in apparent reprisal over informant killings
EVENTS.s: Islamic State Sahel Province fighters attacked at least five localities in the eastern Ménaka region on Sunday 18 October into Monday, killing at least 48 people, two security sources and two local officials told Reuters; provisional tolls ranged from 48 to more than 70 and were still being established on Tuesday 20 October. The sources said the attacks appeared to be retaliation for abuses the previous week by the pro-government MSA militia accompanying the army and Russia's Africa Corps, who allegedly killed about a dozen civilians suspected of informing for ISSP and burned houses. Attackers arrived on dozens of motorcycles, torched homes and stole livestock; some victims died in the fires and others were shot, and hundreds fled to Ménaka town. Tuareg leader and National Transitional Council member Moussa Ag Acharatoumane told AP the 48 dead included children and the elderly. ISSP had not claimed the attack; the Malian military and Russian embassy did not respond.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active conflict. Mali is in open, multi-front war: JNIM has held the Bamako approaches under a renewed fuel blockade since late April and inflicted the heaviest losses on the army in years in September, while ISSP's killing of at least 48 civilians (local tolls 50–70+) in Daoussahak camps around Tagadayat, Ménaka, on 18–19 October, described by Reuters' sources as reprisal for killings of suspected informants by the MSA militia and Africa Corps, shows the IS affiliate escalating in the east and the cycle of atrocity and counter-atrocity tightening, even as ISSP and JNIM fight each other across the Burkina border.

EVENTS.h: Drone strike on West Kordofan transport hub kills 80 after market day
EVENTS.s: A drone struck twice, ten minutes apart, at a transport hub in RSF-held al-Dibab on the evening of 18 October where villagers had gathered after market day to find rides home; a medical source and a witness told AFP 80 people were killed, with 50 bodies buried at the scene and others dying of wounds in al-Mujlad. The RSF's Tasis administration and the Emergency Lawyers group blamed the army, which did not comment; the BBC later cited the Sudan War Observatory as putting the toll at about 150, including a truck carrying some 200 mourners. The UN spokesman condemned the strike on 20 October as part of a 'deeply concerning pattern' of relentless drone attacks.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active conflict. The war is in a drone-dominated phase in which both SAF and RSF strike markets, funerals, displacement camps, dams, power plants and airports far behind the front lines: the 18-19 October wave in West Kordofan, Nyala and Khartoum killed well over 100 by AFP's count, the army's 19 October strike on Abyei's Amiet market (at least 153 dead per local officials) shows it will hit RSF supply lines across the South Sudan border, and the UN reported a 20 October drone strike on the Tendelti power station in White Nile.

EVENTS.adm: Milan (Duomo area), Turin, Bologna, Brescia, Bergamo
EVENTS.h: Two days of rioting and looting in Milan; 271 detained, 500 troops and new security decree
EVENTS.s: Clashes broke out on 17 October around a cost-of-living demonstration in Milan and in Bologna, Brescia, Bergamo and Turin, where police reported 28 arrests; on Sunday 18 October several hundred hooded youths set bins ablaze, looted stores including Decathlon and Vodafone around Piazza Duomo and fought police, who used tear gas and water cannon and detained 271 people, of whom 32 were arrested (23 minors, 13 foreign nationals). Authorities said more than 100 police officers were injured over the two days. On 20 October the cabinet approved a decree deploying 500 additional soldiers to Milan until year-end, creating an offence of violent participation in a demonstration punishable by up to five years, making parents liable for damage by minors and easing prosecution of those over 14.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · avoid city-centre protest zones. Italy has moved from routine strike disruption to sustained violent unrest: the 17-18 October riots in Milan, with clashes in Turin, Bologna, Brescia and Bergamo, injured more than 100 police, and the government responded on 20 October with 500 extra soldiers for Milan and an emergency decree creating new protest offences, while luxury retailers in the centre boarded up.

EVENTS.h: Mortar blast kills at least nine Anti-Threat Security Agency members in Zawiya
EVENTS.s: An 82mm mortar round exploded during a training exercise late on Sunday 18 October at a camp of the Anti-Threat Security Agency, a force under the UN-recognised Government of National Unity, in Zawiya about 40 km west of Tripoli. Libya Alahrar TV, citing medical sources, said at least nine members were killed and several others wounded; there was no immediate comment from authorities, Reuters reported. Zawiya hosts Libya's largest operating refinery and has seen repeated clashes between rival armed groups, including heavy fighting and drone strikes on oil and power infrastructure in August.
EVENTS.impl: No-go for routine travel · essential only with armed escort and air evacuation plan. Libya remains Critical: the 18 October Zawiya mortar blast (at least nine security personnel dead, Reuters) shows how militia and security-force camps embedded in populated areas generate casualties even without active fighting, while UNSMIL's 9 October statement on enforced disappearances in Tripoli and Ghat confirms the kidnap and arbitrary-detention threat to foreigners.

EVENTS.h: Egypt pledges 'all necessary and possible' support to Saudi Arabia against Houthis; parliament vote delayed to 26 Oct
EVENTS.s: After President Sisi on Saturday 17 October called an emergency parliamentary session to authorise military assistance to Saudi Arabia if Riyadh requests it, the presidency said on 18 October, following a National Defence Council meeting attended by the parliamentary speaker, prime minister and army chief, that Egypt would provide 'all necessary and possible forms of support' to defend Saudi security, territorial integrity, resources and holy sites. Reuters reported the move follows intensified Houthi attacks on Riyadh's international airport (13 killed on 10 October, including an Egyptian flight attendant) and Saudi Aramco, and Houthi advances threatening the Bab el-Mandeb shipping route after the collapse of a truce. Parliament postponed the authorisation vote, which needs a two-thirds majority, to 26 October (Reuters, 19 Oct); Sisi has stressed any role would be defensive, and the Houthi-run parliament in Sanaa warned Cairo that intervention would endanger its own security.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · Red Sea/Suez watch; North Sinai and Sudan border restricted. No terrorist attack, Sinai incident or domestic unrest was found in Egypt for 7–21 October, but two developments raise the external-security profile: the 10 October air strike on artisanal gold miners at Jabal al-Uqaydat on the disputed Sudan border (at least 72 dead per Sudanese rights monitors; Egypt's army says it is conducting a sovereignty campaign against illegal mining within its territory) and Cairo's pledge of 'all necessary and possible' support to Saudi Arabia against the Houthis, with a two-thirds parliamentary vote on authorising deployment now set for 26 October (Reuters).

EVENTS.h: Fuel shortage spreads to Niamey; export ban, overnight queues, pumps dry for days
EVENTS.s: Petrol shortages that had hit several regional cities reached the two-million-strong capital on Sunday 18 October, with saturated stations, overnight queues and some station managers saying their tanks had been dry 'for four days', AFP reported. The commerce ministry banned diesel and petrol exports by decree on 12 October to secure domestic supply, and state oil company Sonidep must import petrol; Gen. Tiani sacked Sonidep's managing director in early October without explanation and has ruled out fuel price rises 'so as not to worsen the cost of living'. The Zinder refinery (20,000 bpd) cannot cover demand and the energy ministry recorded a deficit of 196.6 million litres of petrol and 52.6 million litres of diesel over the first eight months of 2026. Moto-taxis and road transport are hardest hit.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · essential travel only with state-level clearance. The first confirmed mass-casualty attack of the window struck the north rather than the jihadist-hit west: gunmen ambushed two escorted passenger buses on the Arlit–Agadez road on 20 October, killing at least 11 (AFP), on the only road corridor used by mining and humanitarian traffic between Agadez and the uranium belt; whether bandits, gold-robbers or anti-junta rebels, the escort failed to prevent it.

EVENTS.h: Opposition PUD alliance reaffirms exiled Machado as leader, tables 14-point transition plan
EVENTS.s: At a meeting in Caracas on Sunday 18 October the Unitary Democratic Platform (PUD), the main opposition alliance, agreed to 'recognise and support the leadership of María Corina Machado' and renewed its demand for free elections, issuing 14 proposals for a democratic transition including freedom for political parties, release of all political prisoners and safe return for exiles; former candidate Edmundo González backed the plan. Machado, in exile since leaving in December 2025 to receive the Nobel Peace Prize and repeatedly blocked from returning according to her party, is excluded from the third round of US-sponsored government-opposition talks that opened in Caracas this month with members of the 2015 National Assembly; the US State Department says the talks are producing reforms. No election date has been set; Machado has told the FT she wants elections by July 2027.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · Caracas workable with advance; stand off from all demonstrations on 22 Oct (opposition from Plaza Venezuela 16:00, PSUV counter-march), low profile, no overland border travel. Venezuela remains in a managed post-Maduro transition rather than a confrontation: since the January 2026 US operation that captured Maduro, the Rodríguez siblings' interim government has reopened the oil sector (oilfield hiring picking up, Reuters 19 Oct), released hundreds of political prisoners, and the US is progressively delisting senior chavistas, most recently National Assembly president Jorge Rodríguez on 14 October (Reuters).

EVENTS.adm: Bay — Buur Hakaba, Berdale, Diinsoor, Aawdiinle, Qansax Dheere
EVENTS.h: Forces loyal to ousted Southwest president hold five Bay towns around Baidoa
EVENTS.s: Military officials said on 17 October that fighters loyal to Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed Laftagareen had taken Berdale, Diinsoor, Buur Hakaba and Qansax Dheere, as well as Aawdiinle about 30 km from Baidoa, leaving the federally backed South West administration without control of most of the state. The takeovers were mostly without fighting; clashes were reported only at Buur Hakaba, which sits on the Mogadishu–Baidoa road. South West Information Minister Nur Sidow Baba said the districts would be brought back under government control, and on 18 October the administration announced a counter-offensive starting with Buur Hakaba. No casualty figures published.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · Mogadishu AAIA/Halane enclave only, contracted advance. Wire-confirmed reporting shows the South West State conflict has widened to the point where Laftagareen-aligned forces hold every major Bay town except Baidoa, including Buur Hakaba on the Mogadishu road, with Ethiopian AU troops standing aside; the federally backed administration announced a counter-offensive on 18 October and Laftagareen on 20 October demanded President Mohamud step aside, so a fight for Baidoa itself is now the base case.

EVENTS.adm: Paris, Lyon, Marseille, Bordeaux, Limoges and other cities
EVENTS.h: 550,000 march against living costs; riots and looting, Limoges city hall burned, 2,397 arrested, 997 police injured
EVENTS.s: A nationwide cost-of-living protest day bringing together students, trade unions, workers, farmers, retirees and Yellow Vest activists drew about 550,000 people by the Interior Ministry's count (800,000 by organisers) and spiralled into the worst rioting in years, with cars burned, barricades and petrol bombs around Place de la République and shops looted in Paris, Marseille, Lyon and other cities; officials said at least 3,000 shops were looted nationwide. Limoges' 1883 Hôtel de Ville was gutted by fire, Lyon's tourist office was set ablaze and the Bordeaux prefect's residence was damaged. Interior Ministry figures put arrests at 2,397 and injuries among police and gendarmes at 997, seven serious, from a deployment of 60,000 officers. President Macron acknowledged failures and rejected Nuñez's offer to resign.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · curfew-aware movement planning. France is the epicentre of the European unrest wave: a month-old student movement fused with cost-of-living anger on 17 October into nationwide rioting that left 997 police injured, 2,397 arrested and at least 3,000 shops looted, prompting the first big-city curfews in years, which were extended on 20 October and are to remain 'as long as necessary'.

EVENTS.adm: Gamboru Ngala–Cameroon border road, Ngala LGA, Borno State
EVENTS.h: Mine and ambush on army patrol convoy near Gamboru Ngala kill 10 soldiers, five CJTF
EVENTS.s: A convoy from a battalion based in Gamboru was patrolling the road between Gamboru Ngala and the Cameroon border on Saturday 17 October when a pickup truck detonated a mine, likely planted by Boko Haram insurgents, killing eight soldiers instantly; gunmen then fired on a second vehicle, killing two more soldiers and five Civilian Joint Task Force members, two soldiers told Reuters. Six wounded soldiers were taken to Maimalari Military Hospital in Maiduguri. Reuters could not independently verify the casualty figures and military spokesman Capt. Mohammed Goni declined to comment. It followed a coordinated assault on an army base in Guzamala LGA on 13 October in which at least 10 soldiers were killed and 20 wounded.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · North-east, Zamfara and Kaduna corridor no-go · Abuja medical watch. The north-east remains in its most dangerous phase in years: Boko Haram/ISWAP overran the Guzamala base on 13 October (at least 10 soldiers killed per Reuters) and killed 10 soldiers and five CJTF in a mine-and-ambush attack on a patrol near Gamboru Ngala on 17 October, despite military claims of more than 100 militants killed in airstrikes.

EVENTS.h: Youth education and cost-of-living protests turn violent in Brussels and Liège
EVENTS.s: Several hundred mostly young people protested in central Brussels on Saturday 17 October against rising education costs and reforms, in unrest partly inspired by France; many wore masks, police used tear gas and water cannon and some protesters overturned a car, a Reuters witness said. A parallel protest took place in Liège, where students clashed with police earlier in the month. Interior Minister Bernard Quintin said what was unfolding was 'no longer mere protest' and that all necessary means would be used to restore order; Belgian media reported about 150 arrests in Brussels, and Defence Minister Theo Francken has since floated a military-trained police reserve for riots.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · strike and protest watch. Belgium is the most exposed of the smaller core states to the French contagion: student-led unrest reached Francophone Belgium in early October and turned violent in Brussels and Liège on 17 October, while union action against the stalled federal budget disrupted the airport, rail and schools on 9 and 12 October.

EVENTS.h: Two arrested for terrorism in Basque Country after seizure of security-force data and suspected arms cache location
EVENTS.s: The Ertzaintza, the Basque regional police, said on 18 October that a 34-year-old Spanish man and a 22-year-old Spanish woman had been arrested on suspicion of terrorism offences after presenting themselves at Irun police station on 17 October. The investigation began with a police check on 26 September at which items seized included information concerning security forces and the potential location of a site containing materials presumed to be weapons and explosives. Both will appear before the National Court; Basque media reported the pair are dissidents of the radical abertzale left and that a third person, an Irish national, is under investigation. The PNV said the news would take the region 'back to past times'.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · weather recovery and protest watch. Spain's immediate risk is environmental: Storm Adam killed at least four people in the Valencia region and Catalonia, alerts were lifted on 20 October and clean-up in Oliva, Pego and the Marina Alta will disrupt road travel for days, with orange warnings lingering in the Balearics.

EVENTS.adm: Baghdad (PMF headquarters, east of the Army Canal)
EVENTS.h: Explosion at PMF headquarters in Baghdad kills one member, wounds four
EVENTS.s: An explosion at the Popular Mobilisation Forces headquarters in Baghdad on 17 October killed one member of the paramilitary group and wounded four others, a security source and a medical source told Reuters. The PMF said a stockpile of obsolete ammunition had exploded, injuring five people and causing a fire that was later brought under control, and Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi ordered an investigation; the PMF later said preliminary forensic findings pointed to an internal malfunction with no evidence of external targeting, although faction-linked lawmakers alleged a drone strike. The PMF is an umbrella of mostly Shi'ite paramilitary factions formally integrated into state security forces, several of them aligned with Iran; the blast came as Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi visited Baghdad and weeks after the 30 September US withdrawal.
EVENTS.impl: Restricted · essential travel with advance, Erbil under drone threat. The Kurdistan Region remains the most active theatre: Iranian drone and missile strikes on Iranian-Kurdish opposition camps in Erbil province were reported on 8, 12, 17 and 21 October (Reuters confirmed the 21 October missile strike north-east of Erbil), none causing reported casualties but all unanswered since coalition air defences left with the 30 September US withdrawal, and on 20 October Tehran's ambassador claimed Baghdad had agreed to expel or hand over the groups, a claim Iraqi officials have not confirmed and the KDPI rejects.

EVENTS.h: UGTT-led march of thousands is biggest anti-Saied protest in years
EVENTS.s: Thousands of Tunisians (AFP put the figure at more than 3,000) marched along Habib Bourguiba Avenue on Saturday 17 October in a protest led by the UGTT labour union with opposition parties from across the spectrum, lawyers, doctors, journalists and civil society, accusing President Saied of undermining democracy and mishandling the economy. Protesters demanded the release of detained critics and an end to attacks on trade-union rights, and revived the 2011 slogan 'the people want the fall of the regime'. Hundreds of police were deployed across the capital and several central roads were closed; Reuters reported no clashes, arrests or injuries. It follows an August 20 rally over prices and shortages.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · avoid central Tunis on protest days. Tunisia's security risk is political rather than kinetic: the 17 October UGTT march was the largest show of opposition to President Saied in years and passed peacefully under heavy policing, but Reuters described it as a rare show of unity across the opposition against a backdrop of water and power cuts, medicine shortages and the detention of government critics (journalist Zied El Heni faced a further terrorism-charge hearing on 16 October).

EVENTS.h: Opposition sweeps Senate runoffs as Babiš's ANO wins no seats
EVENTS.s: Runoff voting on 16-17 October completed the election for one-third of the 81-seat Senate: the pro-European Mayors and Independents won 10 of the 14 seats they contested and the Civic Democrats seven, while PM Andrej Babiš's ANO failed to win any of the seats it contested, a result he called 'catastrophic'. Turnout was low, Reuters assessed the result is unlikely to destabilise the eurosceptic coalition, and ANO still leads national polls after winning six of 13 regional capitals in the concurrent municipal elections. No election-related security incidents were reported.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · routine. No terrorism, sabotage, unrest or major transport disruption was confirmed in Czechia for 7-21 October; the Senate and municipal election cycle ended with a clear opposition win and no reported incidents.

EVENTS.h: Leipzig airport fence breach triggers major police operation; novice driver later admits responsibility
EVENTS.s: Airport staff found a damaged perimeter fence late on Saturday 17 October, triggering an overnight search by federal and Saxony police that closed the north runway while flights continued on the south runway; no vehicle, intruder or suspicious object was found. On Sunday evening two men aged 20 and 32 handed themselves in and admitted driving through the fence while one was practising for a driving test, police said on 19 October. The site was on high alert because an explosives-laden drone was found near a Ukrainian cargo aircraft there in August, an attack Berlin attributed to Russia.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · critical-infrastructure watch. Germany's state-threat environment remains layered: a Hamburg court confirmed Iranian direction of a plot against Jewish leaders, Bulgaria issued European arrest warrants on 19 October for two 19-year-old German nationals over the Starlink antenna arson near Sofia, and German police are holding four people over the Russian-attributed Polish Starlink arson.

EVENTS.h: Abiy names six-month Tigray caretaker government and calls for elections
EVENTS.s: Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's office announced a caretaker administration for Tigray on 16 October, to serve six months, stabilise the region, repair infrastructure, help the displaced return and prepare elections within that period, after the military and the allied Tigray Peace Force took control of large parts of Tigray including Mekelle. A TPLF spokesperson did not immediately respond to Reuters; the TPLF has since rejected the administration. Around 750,000 Tigrayans were still internally displaced as of February according to UNHCR, and Ethiopia has also accused Egypt and Sudan of backing the rebel alliance, which they deny.
EVENTS.impl: No-go north of Addis · Addis essential travel with advance. Four weeks after the TPLF-led alliance's 23 September offensive, federal forces and the allied Tigray Peace Force hold Mekelle, Adigrat, Adwa, Axum and Shire, flights to Mekelle have resumed and Addis has installed a six-month caretaker administration, but the TPLF rejects it, has warned against movement around Tigray's airports and is contesting roads and supply lines in central Tigray, while AFP reports collapsed policing, looting and stabbings in Adigrat and continuing Eritrean presence around Zalambessa.

EVENTS.adm: Nationwide (Rome, Milan, Turin, Bologna and others)
EVENTS.h: 'No Meloni Day' student protests nationwide; bottles and flares thrown at police in Rome, clashes in Turin
EVENTS.s: Students protested nationwide on Friday 16 October over conditions in schools, alongside a teachers' union demanding pay rises and new hires. Thousands rallied outside the education ministry in Rome, where police said bottles and flares were thrown at officers, police clashed with protesters in Turin and schools were occupied in several cities. The protests, partly inspired by movements in France and Spain, came as truck drivers and farmers also mobilised over energy-driven inflation ahead of next year's elections, in what Italian media call an 'autumn of discontent' for PM Giorgia Meloni.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · avoid city-centre protest zones. Italy has moved from routine strike disruption to sustained violent unrest: the 17-18 October riots in Milan, with clashes in Turin, Bologna, Brescia and Bergamo, injured more than 100 police, and the government responded on 20 October with 500 extra soldiers for Milan and an emergency decree creating new protest offences, while luxury retailers in the centre boarded up.

EVENTS.h: EU approves nearly €32m for Estonia's eastern-border drone surveillance system
EVENTS.s: Prime Minister Kristen Michal said at the 16 October European Council in Brussels that Estonia will receive nearly €32m from the EU to strengthen drone surveillance along its eastern border, as leaders also highlighted the Eastern Flank Watch project to improve surveillance, defence and military mobility on the EU's eastern border. Michal also pressed for sufficient eastern-border defence funding and Rail Baltic in the 2028-2034 EU budget talks.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · do not cross into Russia from Narva. No significant security incident occurred on Estonian territory between 7 and 21 October 2026; the most recent notable event remains the August arson attack on Milrem Robotics in Tallinn, which Tallinn attributed to Russian special services on 29 September.

EVENTS.h: Electoral commission sets April–May 2027 polls; opposition, Puntland and Jubaland reject timetable
EVENTS.s: Somalia's electoral commission announced parliamentary elections for 15 April 2027 and a presidential vote for 15 May 2027. Opposition parties and the states of Jubaland and Puntland, which boycotted the March constitutional vote underpinning the timetable, reject it as unilateral; the opposition Somali Future Council restated its rejection on 19 October and warned of further political action. President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's term formally ended earlier this year; the government welcomed the dates and urged all parties to engage in good faith.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · Mogadishu AAIA/Halane enclave only, contracted advance. Wire-confirmed reporting shows the South West State conflict has widened to the point where Laftagareen-aligned forces hold every major Bay town except Baidoa, including Buur Hakaba on the Mogadishu road, with Ethiopian AU troops standing aside; the federally backed administration announced a counter-offensive on 18 October and Laftagareen on 20 October demanded President Mohamud step aside, so a fight for Baidoa itself is now the base case.

EVENTS.h: Pro-government militia claims Eritrean troops retreated with heavy losses; Eritrea calls claims false
EVENTS.s: The pro-government Tigray Peace Force said on 15 October that Eritrean troops had retreated toward the border and 'sustained significant casualties', a claim Eritrea's information minister rejected as false and which could not be independently verified. Photographs obtained by Reuters showed houses damaged by a drone strike during ENDF-TPLF fighting in Rama, near the Eritrean border, on 15 October, as Ethiopian forces expanded control across northern Tigray. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had called for de-escalation in a 14 October call with Abiy, saying the region 'could not tolerate more conflict'.
EVENTS.impl: Avoid · war-risk border state. Eritrea is reported to be a belligerent in the Tigray war: witnesses, a foreign security source and conflict monitors say 5,000-8,000 of its troops crossed through Zalambessa and reached Adigrat in early October, were hit by Ethiopian drones and have largely pulled back toward the border, with AFP reporting on 18 October that Eritrean soldiers remain in Zalambessa on the Ethiopian side while Asmara denies any incursion.

EVENTS.h: Hamburg court jails two for Iran-directed plot to kill German Jewish leaders
EVENTS.s: The Hamburg court sentenced Danish national Ali S. to eight years and six months for preparing an assassination and aggravated arson, finding he had been recruited by Iran's intelligence service to carry out state-sponsored terrorist activity in Germany; Afghan national Tawab M. received four years and six months. In early 2025 S. was tasked with gathering information on Josef Schuster, president of the Central Council of Jews in Germany, and Volker Beck, chairman of the German-Israeli Society, and with spying on two Jewish grocers in Berlin. The verdicts can be appealed; Germany's foreign ministry subsequently summoned the Iranian ambassador.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · critical-infrastructure watch. Germany's state-threat environment remains layered: a Hamburg court confirmed Iranian direction of a plot against Jewish leaders, Bulgaria issued European arrest warrants on 19 October for two 19-year-old German nationals over the Starlink antenna arson near Sofia, and German police are holding four people over the Russian-attributed Polish Starlink arson.

EVENTS.h: FSB arrests Swedish national accused of planning sabotage and 'terrorist acts' for Ukraine
EVENTS.s: The FSB said on 15 October it had detained a 35-year-old Swedish man in Pskov region, near Latvia and Belarus, whom it accuses of serving from February to June as a Ukrainian drone-unit commander in the Aidar Battalion and entering Russia on the pretext of joining the Russian army to carry out sabotage and attacks on military facilities. He has been charged with illegal border crossing and may face terrorism charges; the FSB released a purported confession video in which he gave his name as Freddy Lindholm from Stockholm. Sweden's Foreign Ministry said it was aware of the reports but not yet involved. Two days earlier the FSB detained a Japanese journalist in the Far East on espionage suspicion.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active deep-strike campaign and arbitrary detention. Russia's two principal cities remain under sustained Ukrainian drone attack: the 18 October assault on St Petersburg was the largest yet, killing one, injuring 15 and setting the city's oil terminal ablaze, while Reuters reported a 15 October strike that set fire to the Ryazan refinery feeding Moscow and Russian media reported repeated closures of all four Moscow airports through mid-October.

EVENTS.h: Rio electoral court requests federal troops for 25 October runoff in 15 municipalities
EVENTS.s: On 15 October the Regional Electoral Court (TRE-RJ) voted in plenary to ask the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) to deploy Army, Navy and Air Force personnel for the 25 October presidential runoff, to patrol and support ballot-box logistics in 15 municipalities including Rio de Janeiro, Niterói, Duque de Caxias, Nova Iguaçu, São Gonçalo and Belford Roxo. Court president Cláudio de Mello Tavares wrote that 'the public-security scenario remains unchanged' since the first round and that armed territorial control by criminal factions and militias over voting areas is a 'serious and continuing threat to the free exercise of the vote'. The state government supports the request; federal forces were already deployed in Rio for the 4 October first round. In Rio state only the presidency is on the runoff ballot.
EVENTS.src: Agência Brasil (federal public news agency, reporting TRE-RJ plenary), 15 Oct 2026
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · Rio metro elevated through 25-26 Oct; avoid favela-adjacent routes, Avenida Brasil at night and election-day crowds. Brazil is four days from a polarised presidential runoff (Flávio Bolsonaro 47% vs Lula 45% in the 4 October first round; a bitter first debate on 18 October, per Reuters) in which public security is the dominant issue.

EVENTS.h: EU grants Finland €32m for Border Guard drone detection and counter-drone systems
EVENTS.s: The Interior Ministry announced on 15 October that Finland will receive €32m from the EU Border Management and Visa Instrument to buy drone detection and counter-drone systems for the Border Guard, significantly improving its ability to monitor drones on the eastern border and in the Gulf of Finland and laying the groundwork for countering them. The funding was confirmed in October; procurement falls mainly in 2027-2029.
EVENTS.src: Finnish Ministry of the Interior, 15 Oct 2026
EVENTS.impl: Workable · avoid SE border zone during Russia strike nights. Finland is safe for travel and operations, but the south-eastern coast between Loviisa and the Russian border is subject to short-notice air and sea closures whenever Ukraine mounts large strikes on St Petersburg; Finnish media reported Defence Forces restrictions on 16, 17 and 18 October, lasting up to seven hours, with no drones crossing into Finland.

EVENTS.h: Tsahkna warns Russia will step up hybrid attacks to erode Western support for Ukraine
EVENTS.s: Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna told Reuters on 15 October, on the sidelines of the Warsaw Security Forum, that the risk of Russia eroding Western support for Ukraine through hybrid attacks, sabotage and disinformation is Estonia's key concern. He said the Baltic states, Finland and Poland had prepared for decades for Russian attacks but that Western European societies 'are not ready', and warned Moscow may step up hybrid efforts focused on critical infrastructure and defence-industry companies. The Kremlin denies European allegations of drone, cyber and arson operations in NATO countries.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · do not cross into Russia from Narva. No significant security incident occurred on Estonian territory between 7 and 21 October 2026; the most recent notable event remains the August arson attack on Milrem Robotics in Tallinn, which Tallinn attributed to Russian special services on 29 September.

EVENTS.h: Eritrean troops withdraw from Fatsi toward border as Rubio urges Abiy to de-escalate
EVENTS.s: A Zalambessa resident told AP that Eritrean soldiers withdrew on Monday 12 October from Fatsi, about 20 km from the border town, heading toward Eritrea without fighting, and that Ethiopian federal forces moved into the town later that day. On 14 October Rubio spoke with Abiy urging dialogue under the 2018 peace framework, stressing that all Horn states must respect their neighbours' territorial integrity and avoid cross-border incursions. Ethiopia has told the UN Security Council it is taking self-defence measures against Eritrea, while Eritrea's foreign minister urged the Council to condemn a 'deplorable declaration of war'; Human Rights Watch reported civilians killed by shelling in southern Tigray.
EVENTS.impl: Avoid · war-risk border state. Eritrea is reported to be a belligerent in the Tigray war: witnesses, a foreign security source and conflict monitors say 5,000-8,000 of its troops crossed through Zalambessa and reached Adigrat in early October, were hit by Ethiopian drones and have largely pulled back toward the border, with AFP reporting on 18 October that Eritrean soldiers remain in Zalambessa on the Ethiopian side while Asmara denies any incursion.

EVENTS.h: Police raid opposition broadcaster Halk TV, trustee appointed, broadcasts cut
EVENTS.s: Turkish authorities appointed a government trustee to run pro-opposition broadcaster Halk TV on 14 October as hundreds of police raided its Istanbul office; the channel's live broadcast was cut at 06:30 local time and Editor-in-Chief Suat Toktas was not allowed to continue on air. The Istanbul Chief Prosecutor's Office said its financial crimes unit was investigating chairman Cafer Mahiroglu for bribery, tender-rigging and money laundering; AFP reported 11 people detained under warrants for 17. Opposition leader Ozgur Ozel said 'only dictators' would stage a dawn raid on a TV channel; about 100 people protested outside the Ankara branch and the raid coincided with jailed Istanbul mayor Imamoglu beginning his court defence.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · monitor protests, political flashpoints and flood disruption. No terrorist attack or mass-casualty security incident was recorded in Türkiye in the 7-21 October window; the operational picture was dominated by the 14 October Istanbul flood disaster (eight confirmed dead per AFP on 19 October, roughly 2,000 homes and 900 businesses seriously damaged) and by the deepening political crackdown, with the Halk TV seizure on 14 October, further detentions of opposition mayors in Adana's Cukurova (19 October) and Milas (20 October) corruption probes, and jailed Istanbul mayor Imamoglu's defence under way.

EVENTS.h: Istanbul's heaviest rain since 1942 triggers flash floods; eight dead
EVENTS.s: Torrential rain on 14 October, the heaviest recorded in Istanbul since records began in 1942, triggered flash floods that swept away cars and people, inundated homes and businesses and brought traffic to a near standstill. By 19 October Governor Davut Gul said six people had died in Istanbul, including a 14-year-old boy electrocuted in a puddle, and two more swept away in neighbouring Kocaeli had been found in Pendik, for a toll of eight with one person still missing; the final missing man was found on 20 October, according to state media. Authorities logged about 19,300 damage reports, with some 2,000 homes and 900 businesses seriously damaged, and the interior minister called it the city's worst flood disaster since 1942.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · monitor protests, political flashpoints and flood disruption. No terrorist attack or mass-casualty security incident was recorded in Türkiye in the 7-21 October window; the operational picture was dominated by the 14 October Istanbul flood disaster (eight confirmed dead per AFP on 19 October, roughly 2,000 homes and 900 businesses seriously damaged) and by the deepening political crackdown, with the Halk TV seizure on 14 October, further detentions of opposition mayors in Adana's Cukurova (19 October) and Milas (20 October) corruption probes, and jailed Istanbul mayor Imamoglu's defence under way.

EVENTS.h: US lifts sanctions on Assembly chief Jorge Rodríguez as talks resume
EVENTS.s: On Wednesday 14 October the US Treasury removed Jorge Rodríguez, president of the National Assembly and brother of acting president Delcy Rodríguez, from its sanctions list, a notice on the Treasury website showed; the Venezuelan communications ministry did not immediately comment (Reuters). Rodríguez, 60, has led the legislature since 2021 and heads the government's negotiating team in the US-backed talks with a faction of the opposition, whose third round opened in Caracas the same day; the talks aim to reform the top court and electoral authority ahead of elections. Acting president Rodríguez has promised elections but no firm date is set. Delcy Rodríguez was delisted in April 2026; both were sanctioned in September 2018.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · Caracas workable with advance; stand off from all demonstrations on 22 Oct (opposition from Plaza Venezuela 16:00, PSUV counter-march), low profile, no overland border travel. Venezuela remains in a managed post-Maduro transition rather than a confrontation: since the January 2026 US operation that captured Maduro, the Rodríguez siblings' interim government has reopened the oil sector (oilfield hiring picking up, Reuters 19 Oct), released hundreds of political prisoners, and the US is progressively delisting senior chavistas, most recently National Assembly president Jorge Rodríguez on 14 October (Reuters).

EVENTS.h: NATO chief Rutte visits Tallinn and Ämari, pledges Alliance presence in air, land and sea
EVENTS.s: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte met President Ülle Madise, Prime Minister Kristen Michal, Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna and Defence Minister Martin Herem on 14 October, saying NATO is with Estonia 'in the air, on the ground and at sea' through Allied jets at Ämari, UK-led Forward Land Forces at Tapa and Baltic Sentry at sea. He noted Estonia's core defence spending above 5% of GDP, welcomed a new €10m contribution to the PURL programme for Ukraine, and visited Ämari Air Base, where Turkish Air Force personnel support NATO air defence.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · do not cross into Russia from Narva. No significant security incident occurred on Estonian territory between 7 and 21 October 2026; the most recent notable event remains the August arson attack on Milrem Robotics in Tallinn, which Tallinn attributed to Russian special services on 29 September.

EVENTS.h: Federal forces reach Zalambessa on the Eritrean border after taking Adwa and Axum
EVENTS.s: Ethiopian government troops advanced to Zalambessa, a town of about 15,000 on the Ethiopian side of the Eritrean border previously held by Tigrayan rebels, six sources including people in touch with residents, a diplomat and a conflict expert told Reuters on 13 October. The counter-offensive had driven the TPLF from a string of towns: residents told AFP federal forces and allied militia entered Adwa without resistance on 11 October after overnight looting of the hospital and other institutions, and pro-government forces moved into Shire and Axum. Witnesses and a conflict monitor said Eritrean troops had crossed into Zalambessa the previous week in support of the rebels, which Asmara denies; the UN Security Council held closed-door consultations on the Horn the same day.
EVENTS.impl: No-go north of Addis · Addis essential travel with advance. Four weeks after the TPLF-led alliance's 23 September offensive, federal forces and the allied Tigray Peace Force hold Mekelle, Adigrat, Adwa, Axum and Shire, flights to Mekelle have resumed and Addis has installed a six-month caretaker administration, but the TPLF rejects it, has warned against movement around Tigray's airports and is contesting roads and supply lines in central Tigray, while AFP reports collapsed policing, looting and stabbings in Adigrat and continuing Eritrean presence around Zalambessa.

EVENTS.h: Four civilians killed near Pimbo; traffic on National Road 27 suspended
EVENTS.s: UN OCHA reported on 15 October that four civilians were killed near Pimbo in Djugu territory on Tuesday 13 October, according to local civil society. The attack led to the suspension of traffic along National Road 27, a key humanitarian and commercial corridor, and forced the cancellation of a planned humanitarian mission. OCHA described a broader deterioration in Djugu, where armed attacks and clashes have caused civilian casualties, displaced thousands and disrupted humanitarian activities including the Ebola response; national health authorities reported nearly 9,100 confirmed Ebola cases and more than 4,400 deaths.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · east (Kivus, Ituri) active conflict; Kinshasa workable with advance. The eastern war has entered a new political phase: on 12 October former president Joseph Kabila launched the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN) in Goma, replacing the Rwanda-backed AFC/M23 alliance with M23 leaders Nangaa, Bisimwa and Makenga as his deputies and a declared aim of ending 'tyranny' by force (Reuters); government spokesman Muyaya told AFP on 16 October that Kabila had formalised an 'attack against the Republic', the African Union on 20 October warned against any seizure of power by force, and Congolese media and Africanews report a 15 October interior-ministry ban on the activities of Kabila's PPRD and 12 other parties (not confirmed by a wire outlet).

EVENTS.h: Fifth national day of student protests draws 161,500 by ministry count; violence on fringe of Paris march
EVENTS.s: The high-school movement that began in September over teacher shortages and school conditions held its fifth national mobilisation, joined by university students, teachers and unions; the Interior Ministry counted 161,500 marchers, more than double the previous Thursday, while unions claimed 480,000, with marches in Paris, Nantes, Lyon, Lens, Strasbourg, Toulouse, Bordeaux and Marseille. Most marches were peaceful, but on the fringe of a Paris march masked youths erected barricades, set cars alight and threw objects as police fired tear gas. Police opened 34 internal investigations into alleged violence against demonstrators, one teenager having lost a hand to a stun grenade and another an eye; students rejected a government pledge of 3,000 substitute teachers.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · curfew-aware movement planning. France is the epicentre of the European unrest wave: a month-old student movement fused with cost-of-living anger on 17 October into nationwide rioting that left 997 police injured, 2,397 arrested and at least 3,000 shops looted, prompting the first big-city curfews in years, which were extended on 20 October and are to remain 'as long as necessary'.

EVENTS.h: False hijack alert briefly shuts Nuremberg airport; jets scrambled
EVENTS.s: Nuremberg airport suspended flight operations on 13 October because of an aviation emergency after a Corendon Airlines flight from Corfu transmitted a hijack code and could not be reached by radio; the German air force scrambled two fighter jets to escort it. The airline blamed a radio malfunction, police and the airline said no danger was found, the aircraft landed safely and operations returned to normal. German airports have been on heightened alert since the August drone incident at Leipzig.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · critical-infrastructure watch. Germany's state-threat environment remains layered: a Hamburg court confirmed Iranian direction of a plot against Jewish leaders, Bulgaria issued European arrest warrants on 19 October for two 19-year-old German nationals over the Starlink antenna arson near Sofia, and German police are holding four people over the Russian-attributed Polish Starlink arson.

EVENTS.h: Ex-president Kabila launches FRN front, absorbing AFC/M23 rebellion
EVENTS.s: Former president Joseph Kabila launched a new political-military coalition, the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN), at his Goma residence on 12 October, replacing the AFC/M23 alliance fighting government forces in eastern Congo and taking a more direct role in the insurgency (Reuters). M23 leaders Corneille Nangaa, Bertrand Bisimwa and Sultani Makenga serve as his deputies and the founding declaration pledges to end 'tyranny' by all means 'including force'; Kabila was sentenced to death in absentia in 2025 for treason and denies collaborating with Rwanda. Government spokesman Patrick Muyaya told AFP on 16 October that Kabila had 'decided to formalise his widespread attack against the Republic', and the African Union on 20 October warned against any seizure of power by force.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · east (Kivus, Ituri) active conflict; Kinshasa workable with advance. The eastern war has entered a new political phase: on 12 October former president Joseph Kabila launched the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN) in Goma, replacing the Rwanda-backed AFC/M23 alliance with M23 leaders Nangaa, Bisimwa and Makenga as his deputies and a declared aim of ending 'tyranny' by force (Reuters); government spokesman Muyaya told AFP on 16 October that Kabila had formalised an 'attack against the Republic', the African Union on 20 October warned against any seizure of power by force, and Congolese media and Africanews report a 15 October interior-ministry ban on the activities of Kabila's PPRD and 12 other parties (not confirmed by a wire outlet).

EVENTS.adm: Rhoe displacement site, Djugu territory, Ituri
EVENTS.h: Fighting around Rhoe IDP site kills at least four civilians, health centre burned
EVENTS.s: UN OCHA reported on 13 October that fighting around the Rhoe displacement site in Djugu territory the previous day killed at least four civilians and forced others to flee, according to local civil society. The site hosts more than 50,000 displaced people; a health facility serving more than 5,000 people was burned. OCHA warned the deteriorating security situation in Ituri could further hinder the Ebola response (surveillance, contact tracing, referral of suspected cases) as the outbreak passed 9,000 confirmed cases and 4,300 deaths, and called on all parties to protect civilians and allow humanitarian access.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · east (Kivus, Ituri) active conflict; Kinshasa workable with advance. The eastern war has entered a new political phase: on 12 October former president Joseph Kabila launched the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN) in Goma, replacing the Rwanda-backed AFC/M23 alliance with M23 leaders Nangaa, Bisimwa and Makenga as his deputies and a declared aim of ending 'tyranny' by force (Reuters); government spokesman Muyaya told AFP on 16 October that Kabila had formalised an 'attack against the Republic', the African Union on 20 October warned against any seizure of power by force, and Congolese media and Africanews report a 15 October interior-ministry ban on the activities of Kabila's PPRD and 12 other parties (not confirmed by a wire outlet).

EVENTS.adm: El Bordo toll plaza, Pan-American Highway, Patía, Cauca
EVENTS.h: Car bomb at El Bordo toll booth on Pan-American Highway injures three civilians
EVENTS.s: A car bomb exploded at a toll booth near the town of El Bordo in Cauca department on Monday 12 October, injuring at least three civilians, the army said; the military blamed the Carlos Patiño front of FARC dissidents who rejected the 2016 peace deal. President Abelardo de la Espriella wrote on X: 'I deplore this terrorist attack... along the Panamerican highway. Attacking infrastructure harms people, truck drivers and all of those who need to travel.' AP noted the attack came after the same group killed a sergeant in Timbío on 9 October and an ELN drone strike killed a soldier in La Vega on 10 October, and that the government has cancelled peace talks with the remaining rebel groups, some of which have responded by stepping up attacks on the military.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · Bogotá/Medellín/Cartagena; no-go rural Cauca, Catatumbo, Arauca; avoid Pan-American Highway south of Cali. Under President Abelardo de la Espriella (in office since 7 August) the state is on the offensive and has cancelled peace talks with the remaining rebel groups (AP), and armed groups are answering with an intensifying campaign on the Cauca stretch of the Pan-American Highway: AP confirms a 9 October clash in Timbío in which FARC-dissident Carlos Patiño fighters killed an army sergeant, a 10 October ELN drone strike that killed a soldier in La Vega, and a 12 October car bomb at the El Bordo toll plaza that injured three civilians and closed the highway.

EVENTS.h: PM Burnham says RAF Fairford plot 'almost certainly' directed by Iran's IRGC; ambassador summoned
EVENTS.s: Prime Minister Andy Burnham told Parliament that the 27 September RAF Fairford incident was highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran and almost certainly directed by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband summoned ambassador Seyed Ali Mousavi, who denied any Iranian involvement and demanded evidence, and the Foreign Office announced sanctions on two Iranian nationals. Police have said petrol but no viable explosive was found in the vans seized with the five men arrested near the base.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · elevated state-threat activity. The UK's security picture is dominated by Iranian state-linked activity: the Fairford investigation moved on 20 October to National Security Act rearrests for assisting Iranian intelligence, a separate intrusion at RAF Molesworth is being handled under the same act, and MI5 warned on 13 October that Iran and Russia are stepping up hybrid campaigns.

EVENTS.adm: Mazovia (Wola Krobowska Starlink ground station) / Nürtingen and Berlin, Germany
EVENTS.h: Four detained in Germany over Russian-attributed Starlink station arson in Poland
EVENTS.s: Acting on European arrest warrants issued at Poland's request, German police detained two Turkish citizens on 12 October over the 23 September fire at a Starlink ground station in Wola Krobowska south of Warsaw, which damaged its power system and backup generator but did not knock out the service used by Poland, other Eastern European states and Ukraine's military. PM Donald Tusk called it 'another act of hybrid warfare', intelligence coordinator Tomasz Siemoniak said Warsaw had 'no doubt' Russian intelligence was behind it and that Moscow was increasingly using people with criminal ties, and the suspects face charges of sabotage on behalf of a foreign intelligence service carrying 10 years to life. German police detained two more people on 13 October, bringing the total to four.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · hybrid-threat watch. Poland's window was front-loaded: a cluster of school stabbings that triggered nationwide school security operations, a credible threat against the prime minister with a cache of improvised explosives, and arrests in the Russian-attributed Starlink sabotage case, followed on 16 October by the detention of a 31-year-old Polish-Ukrainian reservist on an officer course in Łódź on spying suspicion.

EVENTS.h: PKK quits four Metina camps as dissolution process advances
EVENTS.s: Turkish security sources said on 12 October that PKK militants had withdrawn from the Hebat, Yajk, Sabri and Sason camps in the Baze district of Iraq's Metina region from 8 October, the first step of an intended disbandment and evidence the peace process is pressing ahead. Turkey's parliament passed a law in August setting the parameters for the PKK's dissolution, providing protections for former militants not implicated in specific crimes and suspended sentences for some convicted of membership. There was no immediate comment from Iraq or the PKK; the process, begun in late 2024, came to a near standstill earlier in 2026 because of the Iran war.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · monitor protests, political flashpoints and flood disruption. No terrorist attack or mass-casualty security incident was recorded in Türkiye in the 7-21 October window; the operational picture was dominated by the 14 October Istanbul flood disaster (eight confirmed dead per AFP on 19 October, roughly 2,000 homes and 900 businesses seriously damaged) and by the deepening political crackdown, with the Halk TV seizure on 14 October, further detentions of opposition mayors in Adana's Cukurova (19 October) and Milas (20 October) corruption probes, and jailed Istanbul mayor Imamoglu's defence under way.

EVENTS.adm: Gardênia Azul, Jacarepaguá, Rio de Janeiro
EVENTS.h: Rio police units fire on each other; BOPE officer killed, five wounded
EVENTS.s: Early on Sunday 11 October two Military Police teams exchanged fire in the Beco do Saci area of the Gardênia Azul community, Jacarepaguá, a few kilometres from the Barra da Tijuca hotel zone. According to the Rio Civil Police, BOPE officers in an unmarked vehicle were stopping the occupants of a car when officers of the Jacarepaguá battalion (18th BPM), in a poorly lit street, mistook them for criminals and a firefight began. BOPE sub-lieutenant Gláucio Marcelo Fonseca da Silva, 54, was dead on arrival at Lourenço Jorge hospital; five other officers were wounded. The Capital Homicide Division seized the weapons for forensic examination and requested body-camera footage; the Military Police internal affairs office opened a separate inquiry. Two lanes of Avenida Ayrton Senna were closed during the incident.
