EVENTS.src: Agência Brasil (federal public news agency, citing Rio Civil Police statement), 12 Oct 2026
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · Rio metro elevated through 25-26 Oct; avoid favela-adjacent routes, Avenida Brasil at night and election-day crowds. Brazil is four days from a polarised presidential runoff (Flávio Bolsonaro 47% vs Lula 45% in the 4 October first round; a bitter first debate on 18 October, per Reuters) in which public security is the dominant issue.

EVENTS.adm: Tibú / El Tarra, Catatumbo, Norte de Santander
EVENTS.h: Air strike on FARC-dissident Frente 33 camp kills four, including 16-year-old
EVENTS.s: At dawn on Sunday 11 October the military bombed a camp of the Frente 33 FARC-dissident faction in the Catatumbo region bordering Venezuela, in an operation President Abelardo de la Espriella said he personally ordered. Defence Minister Jorge Mora said on Monday that three men and a 16-year-old girl were killed and that three soldiers were 'gravely affected as a result of a minefield' when ground troops entered the site; troops seized ten rifles, a machine gun and ammunition. AFP reported it was the fourth bombing raid ordered since de la Espriella took office in August, bringing the toll of those raids to 46 suspected guerrillas including seven minors. Frente 33 and the ELN have been fighting each other in Catatumbo since January 2025, using explosive drones and mines, with more than 120,000 people displaced.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · Bogotá/Medellín/Cartagena; no-go rural Cauca, Catatumbo, Arauca; avoid Pan-American Highway south of Cali. Under President Abelardo de la Espriella (in office since 7 August) the state is on the offensive and has cancelled peace talks with the remaining rebel groups (AP), and armed groups are answering with an intensifying campaign on the Cauca stretch of the Pan-American Highway: AP confirms a 9 October clash in Timbío in which FARC-dissident Carlos Patiño fighters killed an army sergeant, a 10 October ELN drone strike that killed a soldier in La Vega, and a 12 October car bomb at the El Bordo toll plaza that injured three civilians and closed the highway.

EVENTS.h: Man detained over plot against PM Tusk and defence minister; improvised explosives seized
EVENTS.s: Police detained 66-year-old Krzysztof N. on Sunday 11 October on suspicion of planning an attack on PM Donald Tusk and Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz after police received information about a possible attack and improvised explosive materials were found in his apartment. Warsaw prosecutors charged him on 13 October with nine offences, the most serious being plotting to forcibly overthrow state authorities using stockpiled explosives, punishable by 2-15 years, plus promoting the violent seizure of power, promoting war including the one in Ukraine and inciting hatred; he had sought recruits and built an online group of several hundred people. He refused to explain himself and a court was to rule on his custody on 14 October.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · hybrid-threat watch. Poland's window was front-loaded: a cluster of school stabbings that triggered nationwide school security operations, a credible threat against the prime minister with a cache of improvised explosives, and arrests in the Russian-attributed Starlink sabotage case, followed on 16 October by the detention of a 31-year-old Polish-Ukrainian reservist on an officer course in Łódź on spying suspicion.

EVENTS.adm: Oran (arrests) / El Kala border zone, El Tarf
EVENTS.h: Algeria says it arrested 61 Moroccans suspected of preparing 'acts of sabotage'
EVENTS.s: Algeria's General Directorate of National Security (DGSN) announced on Sunday 11 October that judicial police in Oran had dismantled an 'international Moroccan criminal network' of 61 Moroccan nationals, including a former Moroccan soldier, arrested in early October on suspicion of preparing acts of sabotage undermining security and public order. The DGSN said the group flew to Tunis and entered Algeria clandestinely via mountain trails near El Kala, close to the Tunisian border, before travelling overland to Oran; passports and cash in dirhams and euros were seized and the suspects were referred to the specialised criminal prosecutor in Oran. The statement gave no detail of the alleged plots, no weapons seizure was announced and the allegations have not been tested in court; Rabat has made no official response. Diplomatic relations have been severed since August 2021 and the land border closed since 1994.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · southern and eastern border zones restricted. No terrorist attack, clash or significant protest was confirmed in Algeria for 7–21 October; the environment is stable but heavily securitised and the state continues to frame domestic problems (summer wildfires, migration networks) as foreign-backed subversion.

EVENTS.h: Federal forces re-enter Adigrat after drone strikes push back Eritrean troops
EVENTS.s: Ethiopian government forces and allied militia entered Adigrat, 30 km from the Eritrean border, on the morning of 10 October, three residents told Reuters, days after Eritrean troops were pushed back from the city. Residents reported many drone strikes near Adigrat on 7-9 October that destroyed Eritrean lorries and were followed by an Eritrean withdrawal northward; Reuters could not independently verify the incursion, which Asmara denies. Ethiopia told the Security Council Eritrean troops had advanced up to 60 km inside Tigray and that it had no option but to defend itself, while Eritrea asked the Council for Chapter VII 'deterrent measures' against Ethiopia.
EVENTS.impl: No-go north of Addis · Addis essential travel with advance. Four weeks after the TPLF-led alliance's 23 September offensive, federal forces and the allied Tigray Peace Force hold Mekelle, Adigrat, Adwa, Axum and Shire, flights to Mekelle have resumed and Addis has installed a six-month caretaker administration, but the TPLF rejects it, has warned against movement around Tigray's airports and is contesting roads and supply lines in central Tigray, while AFP reports collapsed policing, looting and stabbings in Adigrat and continuing Eritrean presence around Zalambessa.

EVENTS.adm: Jabal al-Uqaydat, Egypt–Sudan border (Halayeb area / Sudan's River Nile State)
EVENTS.h: Air strikes on gold-mining site near Sudan border kill at least 72, rights group says
EVENTS.s: At least 72 artisanal gold miners were killed and more than 50 wounded in air strikes on Saturday 10 October at Jabal al-Uqaydat, a mountainous mining area straddling the disputed Egypt–Sudan border, the Khartoum-based Emergency Lawyers group said, blaming Egyptian military aircraft and saying the strike fell inside Sudanese territory; AFP and Al Jazeera could not independently verify the account. Egypt's military did not directly address the allegation but said on 12 October that the armed forces and police were conducting a campaign against illegal gold mining, migration and smuggling near the Sudanese border 'within Egyptian territory', after dropping warning leaflets. Sudan's army chief Burhan ordered a fact-finding inquiry; it is the second reported strike on the site this year after one in June that reportedly killed 23. Two Egyptian truck drivers were separately shot dead in Khartoum around 11–12 October and Egyptian hauliers suspended trips into Sudan.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · Red Sea/Suez watch; North Sinai and Sudan border restricted. No terrorist attack, Sinai incident or domestic unrest was found in Egypt for 7–21 October, but two developments raise the external-security profile: the 10 October air strike on artisanal gold miners at Jabal al-Uqaydat on the disputed Sudan border (at least 72 dead per Sudanese rights monitors; Egypt's army says it is conducting a sovereignty campaign against illegal mining within its territory) and Cairo's pledge of 'all necessary and possible' support to Saudi Arabia against the Houthis, with a two-thirds parliamentary vote on authorising deployment now set for 26 October (Reuters).

EVENTS.adm: Gwashi–Nasarawa road, Bukkuyum LGA, Zamfara State
EVENTS.h: Bandits ambush military-escorted traders' convoy in Zamfara, killing at least 20
EVENTS.s: Gunmen ambushed a convoy of traders travelling under military escort from Gwashi to Nasarawa market in Bukkuyum district at about 2 p.m. on Saturday 10 October, killing at least 20 people, a witness and a military source told Reuters. Local resident Musa Danladi, who helped retrieve the bodies, said four soldiers, three policemen and a civil defence officer were among the dead alongside 12 civilians; a military source confirmed the attack and said 19 people were also wounded. Military and police authorities did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The attack came days after Reuters relayed unverified accounts of bandits killing at least 25 soldiers at a camp in Bindin, Maru LGA, on 5 October.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · North-east, Zamfara and Kaduna corridor no-go · Abuja medical watch. The north-east remains in its most dangerous phase in years: Boko Haram/ISWAP overran the Guzamala base on 13 October (at least 10 soldiers killed per Reuters) and killed 10 soldiers and five CJTF in a mine-and-ambush attack on a patrol near Gamboru Ngala on 17 October, despite military claims of more than 100 militants killed in airstrikes.

EVENTS.h: Eritrea asks UNSC for Chapter VII 'deterrent measures' against Ethiopia
EVENTS.s: Foreign Minister Osman Saleh wrote to the Security Council on 10 October asking it to 'forcefully condemn Ethiopia's deplorable declaration of war against Eritrea' and take 'the requisite deterrent measures' under Chapter VII, in a letter seen by Reuters; he did not specify which measures. The letter came a day after Ethiopia told Council members Eritrean troops had advanced up to 60 km into Tigray and that it had no option but to defend itself. Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel said Eritrea had shown restraint and that Ethiopia's 2023 pledge to acquire sovereign sea access amounted to declaring a war of aggression; Reuters could not independently verify the incursion, which Asmara denies.
EVENTS.impl: Avoid · war-risk border state. Eritrea is reported to be a belligerent in the Tigray war: witnesses, a foreign security source and conflict monitors say 5,000-8,000 of its troops crossed through Zalambessa and reached Adigrat in early October, were hit by Ethiopian drones and have largely pulled back toward the border, with AFP reporting on 18 October that Eritrean soldiers remain in Zalambessa on the Ethiopian side while Asmara denies any incursion.

EVENTS.h: RSF drone strike on displaced camp near Ethiopian border kills 41
EVENTS.s: A drone attack blamed on the Rapid Support Forces hit a camp for displaced people in the Abu Shandi area of Blue Nile state on Friday 9 October, killing 41 people including eight children and many women, according to the Emergency Lawyers group. The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs said it was 'appalled by horrifying reports', that most casualties were women and children, and that the area had been under sustained attack in recent weeks. An RSF spokesperson did not respond to a request for comment.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active conflict. The war is in a drone-dominated phase in which both SAF and RSF strike markets, funerals, displacement camps, dams, power plants and airports far behind the front lines: the 18-19 October wave in West Kordofan, Nyala and Khartoum killed well over 100 by AFP's count, the army's 19 October strike on Abyei's Amiet market (at least 153 dead per local officials) shows it will hit RSF supply lines across the South Sudan border, and the UN reported a 20 October drone strike on the Tendelti power station in White Nile.

EVENTS.h: Intercommunal street battles in Rumbek kill 71 before security forces regain control
EVENTS.s: Fighting between armed youths from neighbouring communities spread into the Lakes State capital at about 04:00 on 9 October, with heavy machine-gun fire and running street battles in the town. The caretaker information ministry said at least 71 people were killed, including four soldiers, before reinforced SSPDF, police and National Security forces regained control from outsiders who had briefly tried to take the town; four armed civilians were arrested. UNMISS later stepped up patrols and protection of the state hospital, airport and aid compounds.
EVENTS.impl: No-go outside Juba · essential travel only. South Sudan is now absorbing direct spillover from Sudan's drone war: the 19 October Amiet market strike in Abyei, which a Sudanese officer told AP targeted RSF-bound fuel tankers, is the deadliest single incident in the country this year and signals that supply corridors through South Sudanese territory will be targeted again; Juba has summoned Sudan's ambassador but has no means to deter further strikes.

EVENTS.h: UN Humanitarian Coordinator warns of escalating violence in Baidoa, calls for de-escalation
EVENTS.s: Humanitarian Coordinator George Conway said he was gravely concerned by escalating violence in Baidoa, which was forcing people to flee and undermining access to services in a city facing an increased risk of famine, high child malnutrition and projected El Niño floods. He called on all parties to de-escalate, protect civilians and humanitarian personnel, and allow unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Baidoa. UNHCR separately recorded more than 5,600 people displaced by the 28 September clashes in the city.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · Mogadishu AAIA/Halane enclave only, contracted advance. Wire-confirmed reporting shows the South West State conflict has widened to the point where Laftagareen-aligned forces hold every major Bay town except Baidoa, including Buur Hakaba on the Mogadishu road, with Ethiopian AU troops standing aside; the federally backed administration announced a counter-offensive on 18 October and Laftagareen on 20 October demanded President Mohamud step aside, so a fight for Baidoa itself is now the base case.

EVENTS.h: Overcrowded migrant boat sinks off Obock; at least 139 dead, 84 missing
EVENTS.s: A boat carrying 305 mostly Ethiopian migrants bound for Yemen capsized north of Obock on the night of 8-9 October. The IOM said on 11 October that at least 139 people, including at least 15 children, had died and about 84 were missing, with more than 80 survivors, all Ethiopian nationals, taken to its Migrant Response Centre in Obock; its chief of mission said local authorities were overwhelmed by the bodies washing ashore. IOM described it as one of the deadliest shipwrecks recorded on the Eastern Route from the Horn of Africa to the Arabian Peninsula, and had warned on 6 October that Djibouti faces 'overlapping emergencies' with more than 3,700 Yemeni refugees arriving in three weeks.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · transit hub. No violent security incident was recorded inside Djibouti in the past 14 days; the only major event was the 9 October migrant shipwreck off Obock, one of the deadliest on record on the Eastern Route, against a backdrop of thousands of Yemeni refugees arriving at Obock and migrants stranded in the desert.

EVENTS.h: Army sergeant killed in clash with FARC-dissident Carlos Patiño front on Pan-American Highway
EVENTS.s: On Friday 9 October troops clashed with fighters of the Carlos Patiño front (FARC dissidents who rejected the 2016 peace deal) in the municipality of Timbío on the Pan-American Highway south of Popayán, killing a sergeant, according to the army (AP, 12 Oct). The following day, 10 October, a drone attack on a military patrol killed a soldier in La Vega, also in Cauca, which the army blamed on the ELN. The two incidents preceded the 12 October car bomb at the El Bordo toll plaza on the same highway.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · Bogotá/Medellín/Cartagena; no-go rural Cauca, Catatumbo, Arauca; avoid Pan-American Highway south of Cali. Under President Abelardo de la Espriella (in office since 7 August) the state is on the offensive and has cancelled peace talks with the remaining rebel groups (AP), and armed groups are answering with an intensifying campaign on the Cauca stretch of the Pan-American Highway: AP confirms a 9 October clash in Timbío in which FARC-dissident Carlos Patiño fighters killed an army sergeant, a 10 October ELN drone strike that killed a soldier in La Vega, and a 12 October car bomb at the El Bordo toll plaza that injured three civilians and closed the highway.

EVENTS.h: Union protest and public-sector strike against budget cuts disrupt flights, rail and schools
EVENTS.s: Thousands joined a national union demonstration in Brussels on Friday 9 October against planned federal budget cuts, ending with a small group clashing with police, who used tear gas and water cannon; Brussels Airport expected about 140 flight cancellations because ground handler Alyzia was short-staffed and De Lijn and STIB services were curtailed. A second nationwide public-sector strike on Monday 12 October disrupted rail, public transport, public broadcasting and schools as PM Bart De Wever's coalition missed its budget deadline and he cancelled his State of the Union address. Belgian media reported the deal could slip to late October or early November, straining coalition cohesion.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · strike and protest watch. Belgium is the most exposed of the smaller core states to the French contagion: student-led unrest reached Francophone Belgium in early October and turned violent in Brussels and Liège on 17 October, while union action against the stalled federal budget disrupted the airport, rail and schools on 9 and 12 October.

EVENTS.h: UNSMIL voices deep concern over enforced disappearances and abductions in Tripoli and Ghat
EVENTS.s: UNSMIL said on 9 October it was deeply concerned by recent reports of enforced disappearances, arbitrary detention and abductions in Libya, citing the disappearance of Dr Mohamed Sharafeddine Al-Fituri and Abu Bakr Al-Jarrari in Tripoli and the arbitrary arrest of Mustafa Al-Sheikh and Mohammed Al-Sheikh in Ghat, whose whereabouts were unknown. The mission called on authorities to establish their fate, release anyone unlawfully held or refer them to judicial authorities, and investigate all allegations impartially. The statement confirms the kidnap and arbitrary-detention risk that persists in western and southern Libya despite the Tripoli de-escalation arrangements. (A militia ammunition-depot explosion in Misrata's Yadr district the same day, reported by Libyan outlets, could not be wire-confirmed.)
EVENTS.impl: No-go for routine travel · essential only with armed escort and air evacuation plan. Libya remains Critical: the 18 October Zawiya mortar blast (at least nine security personnel dead, Reuters) shows how militia and security-force camps embedded in populated areas generate casualties even without active fighting, while UNSMIL's 9 October statement on enforced disappearances in Tripoli and Ghat confirms the kidnap and arbitrary-detention threat to foreigners.

EVENTS.h: King says migration cooperation model with Spain has reached its limit
EVENTS.s: Opening parliament on Friday 9 October, King Mohammed VI said Morocco's efforts to curb irregular migration had produced concrete results but that the current cooperation model with Spain had reached its limits amid recurring crises, citing 'obsolete' Spanish court decisions that impede repatriation of minors and 'fake asylum seekers'. He said the partnership with Madrid was a sovereign choice that 'will never be subject to any pressure, threat, or blackmail'. At least 70,000 people crossed from Morocco into Ceuta on 30–31 July; most returned but thousands, including minors, remain, and the crisis dominates Spain's 29 November election campaign.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · open for business. Morocco recorded no security incident in the 7–21 October window that could be confirmed by a wire service; the only candidate item, a 12 October gathering in Rabat for hunger-striking Gdeim Izik prisoners that police dispersed, is reported by NGO and Moroccan sources only and is not carried in the feed.

EVENTS.h: Three school attacks in four days kill custodian, wound 14; 76 detained nationwide
EVENTS.s: On 7 October a 19-year-old student at Vocational School Complex No. 4 in Ostrołęka attacked fellow students, teachers and passers-by with a sharp object, wounding nine; on 8 October a 15-year-old killed a school custodian and wounded two adults in a knife attack at his former school in Leszczydół-Nowiny in the same province; and on 10 October a 21-year-old woman wounded three people at a private post-secondary school in Warsaw's Praga district. Police detained 76 people nationwide and checked nearly 50,000 schools, and 59 schools pre-emptively suspended classes on 9 October over 'bloody Friday' rumours; the government found no evidence of an online challenge and no confirmation the attacks were linked. PM Tusk blamed online glorification of violence.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · hybrid-threat watch. Poland's window was front-loaded: a cluster of school stabbings that triggered nationwide school security operations, a credible threat against the prime minister with a cache of improvised explosives, and arrests in the Russian-attributed Starlink sabotage case, followed on 16 October by the detention of a 31-year-old Polish-Ukrainian reservist on an officer course in Łódź on spying suspicion.

EVENTS.h: Two Latvian men arrested inside US/NATO intelligence base after fence breach
EVENTS.s: Ministry of Defence Police found an abandoned vehicle outside RAF Molesworth late on 7 October and, after a small breach of the perimeter fence was identified, two UK-resident Latvian nationals aged 36 and 32 were arrested inside the base. They were initially held for trespass and criminal damage and then further arrested under section 4 of the National Security Act 2023 for entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the UK; Counter Terrorism Policing said there was nothing to link it to the RAF Fairford case. Both were released on bail on 9 October. Molesworth hosts the NATO Intelligence Fusion Centre and US intelligence operations centres for Europe and Africa.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · elevated state-threat activity. The UK's security picture is dominated by Iranian state-linked activity: the Fairford investigation moved on 20 October to National Security Act rearrests for assisting Iranian intelligence, a separate intrusion at RAF Molesworth is being handled under the same act, and MI5 warned on 13 October that Iran and Russia are stepping up hybrid campaigns.

EVENTS.h: Four Ukrainians arrested in Vienna on spying suspicion; two journalists released
EVENTS.s: Austrian police arrested two Ukrainian men on 5 October on suspicion of espionage; the APA news agency reported they were suspected members of Ukrainian military intelligence and a court remanded them in custody. On 8 October masked officers detained Ukrainska Pravda investigative reporter Mykhailo Tkach and cameraman Yaroslav Bondarenko, who were tracking fugitive former Ukrainian prosecutor general Ruslan Kravchenko; Bondarenko was injured by broken glass during the arrest. Both were released after more than 12 hours, and Vienna prosecutors said on 12 October the arrest was ordered because they had been seen watching a location the two suspects had also surveilled, not because of their profession.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · routine. Austria recorded no significant security incident in the window; the only notable event is the Vienna counter-espionage case, in which two Ukrainians remain in pre-trial custody (Austrian media report it has been extended to 20 November) after two Ukrainian journalists were briefly swept up and released.

ADVS.t: Nigeria — first Ebola case in Abuja: screening and evacuation cover
ADVS.b: Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola (Bundibugyo) case in more than a decade on 20 October: a woman who arrived in Abuja via Addis Ababa on 5 October and was admitted to a private hospital on 11 October with malaria-like symptoms (Reuters, AP, DW). Authorities are tracing 44 contacts, most of them healthcare workers; there is no approved vaccine or treatment for this species, and the outbreak has killed more than 4,600 people since May. No travel restrictions are in force and the security picture in Abuja and Lagos is unchanged.
pts: Confirm medical-evacuation cover and the receiving facility for every principal in Abuja and Lagos before travel; private hospitals in Abuja are the exposure point so far
Brief principals on symptom reporting and avoiding non-essential clinic visits; carry a 72-hour medical kit
Expect entry screening and possible route changes at Nnamdi Azikiwe and Murtala Muhammed airports; build slack into transfers
Trigger for posture review: any secondary case, a healthcare-worker infection, or a case outside Abuja

ADVS.t: Western Europe — protest, curfew and strike disruption (France, Italy, Belgium)
ADVS.b: Current as of 21 October 2026. France extended night curfews in Paris and other major cities on 20 October after the 17 October cost-of-living marches turned to rioting (2,513 in custody), with troops assigned static roles for the 24 October protest day; Milan saw two days of rioting and looting (271 detained) and a 20 October cabinet decree sends 500 troops to the city to year-end; Belgian education and budget protests turned violent in Brussels and Liège (195 arrested) and a national union day cancelled ~140 Brussels Airport flights. Haulier blockades are causing fuel shortages in southern Italy.
pts: Check curfew hours and protest calendars before any evening movement in Paris, Milan, Turin, Rome or Brussels
Pre-book ground transport and build a 24-hour slip into itineraries through Brussels and Italian hubs on announced strike days
Screen venue-adjacent accommodation for protest-zone exposure; avoid city-centre squares on announced march days
Fuel: full tanks before entering southern Italy while blockades run

ADVS.b: Current as of 21 October 2026. Al-Shabaab activity in the capital is at its lowest level in years and is now low-lethality harassment of checkpoints on the western (Afgooye-corridor) districts, mostly overnight. The threats that reach the airport enclave are different: indirect fire — seven mortar barrages on AAIA and Halane between January 2024 and May 2025, one of them lethal, none since — and government–opposition confrontation, which reached the AAIA perimeter in June 2026 and is building again: the federal government has lost most of South West State to forces loyal to the ousted regional president (AFP, 17 Oct), set a contested May 2027 presidential election that Puntland, Jubaland and the opposition reject (AFP, 15 Oct), and, per Somali local reporting not independently confirmed, says it removed 260 armed guards from opposition leaders’ residences on 13 October.
pts: Movement limited to the AAIA/Halane enclave and the airport road, with contracted armed advance; no movement into Hodan, Daynile or the Afgooye corridor
Indirect-fire drills and hard cover current for every principal in the enclave; last barrage cadence was four in nine weeks (Apr–May 2025)
In-place plan that does not depend on the airport road being open, with 72 hours of self-sufficiency
Trigger for posture review: armed convoys entering Wadajir or Waaberi, security forces surrounding opposition residences, or any mortar fire anywhere in Banaadir
Sanctions screening re-run on any counterparty with South West State or Laftagareen links (federal designations reported locally, 13 Oct)

ADVS.b: Current as of 21 October 2026. Mali (ISSP massacre of 48 civilians in Ménaka, 18 Oct), Niger (gunmen killed at least 11 on two escorted passenger buses outside Agadez, 20 Oct), Sudan (drone strikes killing ~80 in West Kordofan and 17 in Nyala, 18–19 Oct), South Sudan (153 reported killed at Abyei market, 19 Oct), northern Ethiopia and Eritrea (federal–TPLF fighting, Eritrean units still at Zalambessa) and eastern DRC remain outside the TCG movement envelope. Requirements in these jurisdictions are referred, not accepted, unless a dedicated advance and armed local capability are contracted in writing.
pts: No principal movement without contracted local armed support
Written client acknowledgement of residual risk before mobilisation
Medical evacuation route confirmed and funded before deployment — Djibouti and Nairobi remain the staging assumption
Sanctions screening on every local counterparty

ADVS.t: Kurdistan Region — drone threat to Erbil and flight contingency
ADVS.b: Four Iranian strikes in two weeks on Iranian Kurdish opposition sites in Erbil province — drones west of Erbil on 8, 12 and 17 Oct, and missile or drone fire on a PAK camp in the Balisan mountains north-east of the city on 21 Oct (Reuters) — plus an explosion at a PMF headquarters in Baghdad (17 Oct). Tehran says Baghdad has agreed to expel or hand over the opposition groups (20 Oct). Commercial schedules into Erbil remain exposed to short-notice airspace closures.
pts: Build a 24-hour slip into inbound itineraries
Confirm ground assets independently of flight status
Avoid the western and north-eastern approaches to Erbil (Koya, Zrgwez and Balisan camp areas) where strikes have landed
Brief principals on overland alternatives via Türkiye before departure

ADVS.t: Russia and the Baltic–Nordic frontier — hybrid and deep-strike exposure
ADVS.b: Russia: largest drone attack yet on St Petersburg (18 Oct), all four Moscow airports closed up to seven hours (16 Oct), and a Swedish national arrested by the FSB on sabotage charges (15 Oct) — detention risk for Western nationals is arbitrary. Finland closed Gulf of Finland air and sea zones twice over stray-drone risk (18 Oct); an Estonian ex-soldier is held by the FSB after crossing from Narva.
pts: Russia is no-go for TCG principals; no overland crossings from Narva or the Finnish south-east
Expect short-notice closures of Finnish and Estonian coastal airspace on Russian strike nights
Treat GPS degradation as standard in the Gulf of Finland and eastern Baltic
Brief dual nationals and anyone with prior military service on arbitrary-detention exposure

ADVS.t: Kenya — Ebola screening and Level 3 advisory
ADVS.b: The United States raised Kenya to Level 3 (reconsider travel) on 19 October over Ebola, crime and terrorism; Kenya confirmed a ninth Ebola case on 20 October, all linked to the index patient, with no community transmission reported. An IED killed two police officers near Hagadera, Garissa, on 9 October. Nairobi remains the regional hub and staging node.
pts: Health screening and medical-evacuation cover confirmed for every principal transiting Nairobi
No movement into Garissa, Mandera, Wajir or Lamu counties
Brief principals against unvetted ride-hailing and after-dark solo movement in Nairobi

OUTLOOK.a: Core Europe is in a two-track deterioration over the 90-day horizon. The cost-of-living and education protest wave that exploded in France on 17 October has produced the worst rioting in years in France and Italy and violent spillover in Belgium, and with a French national protest day on 24 October, a French strike on 5 November, Italy's 20 November general strike and Belgium's unresolved budget, periodic urban disorder in Paris, Lyon, Marseille, Milan and Brussels is the base case through December. In parallel, the Iranian campaign against military and Jewish targets in Britain and Germany and the Russian sabotage campaign against Starlink and defence-supply infrastructure in Poland, Germany and Bulgaria continue at a steady tempo, with Moscow signalling, per WSJ reporting, that Leipzig will not be the last target. Central Europe (Czechia, Slovakia, Austria) stays low-risk, and Spain's main shock was meteorological.
dr: Energy-driven inflation from the Iran war feeding student, union, trucker and Yellow Vest mobilisation, with governments in France, Italy and Belgium constrained by debt and unable to buy social peace
Iranian state-directed plotting via criminal proxies against US-linked bases and Jewish/Israeli targets in the UK and Germany, now producing National Security Act arrests and court convictions
Russian hybrid sabotage of Ukraine-supporting infrastructure (Starlink ground stations, airports, drone and defence plants) using disposable foreign recruits, concentrated in Poland and Germany
ind: Scale and violence of the 24 October French protest day and whether curfews spread beyond Paris, Lyon, Lille, Nice and Marseille or escalate to a state of emergency
Whether Milan stays calm under the troop deployment and new decree, and whether Belgian budget deadlock triggers the pencilled-in late-November general strike
Charges in the RAF Fairford case, further sabotage at Starlink or airport sites in Poland/Germany, and any attack on Jewish or Israeli venues following the Hamburg verdict
OUTLOOK.im: Journey managers should treat Paris, Lyon, Marseille, Lille, Milan and Brussels as protest-cycle cities through the autumn, routing movements away from centres on announced protest days and building curfew-aware itineraries, and should keep client sites near US military installations, Jewish community facilities and Ukraine-linked logistics under enhanced monitoring across the UK, Germany and Poland.

OUTLOOK.a: Over the next 90 days the Nordic-Baltic states will stay safe for corporate travel while absorbing the spill-over of an intensifying Ukraine-Russia deep-strike war: each large Ukrainian raid on St Petersburg now triggers multi-hour air and sea closures on Finland's south-east coast, and stray-drone, GNSS-jamming and sabotage risks persist along the whole eastern flank. The 20-21 October Oslo and St Petersburg talks open a diplomatic track, but neither side has paused strikes and a ceasefire before year-end is uncertain. Russia itself will remain a no-go environment with escalating strike intensity, chronic airport disruption and politically motivated detentions of Westerners. The most likely change is a sharper Russian hybrid response against Baltic and Nordic infrastructure or defence firms as Western sanctions tighten.
dr: Ukrainian long-range drone campaign on St Petersburg, Moscow and refineries, now exceeding 1,000 drones per night, driving Finnish airspace closures and stray-drone risk
Russian hybrid pressure on NATO's northern flank: espionage, sabotage of defence firms, GNSS interference and sanctioned shadow-fleet traffic along the Norwegian and Baltic coasts
Trajectory of US-brokered talks after the Oslo and St Petersburg meetings, which will determine whether strike intensity falls or both sides escalate to improve negotiating positions
ind: Frequency and duration of Finnish Defence Forces restriction areas in the eastern Gulf of Finland, and any drone actually crossing into Finnish or Estonian territory
New arson, sabotage or cyber incidents attributed to Russian services against Baltic or Nordic infrastructure and defence contractors, following the Milrem attack
Announcement of a trilateral US-Russia-Ukraine meeting or energy ceasefire, versus further record drone raids on St Petersburg and Moscow airport closures
OUTLOOK.im: Maintain normal travel for Norway, Finland and Estonia with advance notice for Finland's south-east coast and an absolute bar on crossing into Russia; keep Russia at no-go, with independent overland exit plans via the Baltics for any residual staff.

OUTLOOK.a: Over the next 90 days the region will be shaped by Iran's post-US-withdrawal freedom of action in Iraq rather than by domestic militancy in Türkiye. Iranian strikes on opposition camps in Erbil province are now near-weekly and Tehran is using the joint security commission to press Baghdad for expulsions; whether Iraq complies, stalls or sees the groups relocate deeper into the KRI will determine if strike geography widens toward Erbil city, its airport and Western-operated oil assets as it did in 2025. Türkiye's PKK dissolution is the one clearly improving line, lowering the southeastern insurgent threat, while the political crackdown, the Imamoglu trial and COP31 in November make protest and heavy policing in Istanbul and Ankara the dominant disruptor; Baghdad remains High on militia-depot blasts, Islamic State hit-and-run attacks around Kirkuk and the pro-Iran realignment of the security establishment.
dr: Iranian drone and missile strikes on Iranian-Kurdish opposition camps in Erbil and Sulaimaniyah provinces with no coalition air defence since the 30 September US withdrawal
Tehran's pressure on Baghdad and Erbil to expel or hand over opposition groups via the Iraq-Iran joint security commission, and Baghdad's drift toward Iran-aligned security leadership
Türkiye's domestic political crackdown (opposition mayors, Halk TV, Imamoglu trial) against the backdrop of an advancing PKK dissolution and the November COP31 summit
ind: Any Iranian strike landing within Erbil city limits, near Erbil International Airport or on a Western oil facility, or a strike causing fatalities
An Iraqi government or KRG statement confirming expulsion or relocation of Iranian-Kurdish groups, or the groups resisting relocation by force
A PKK statement reversing withdrawals, a Turkish cross-border operation in Iraq, or mass arrests at Istanbul or Ankara demonstrations around the Imamoglu trial or COP31
OUTLOOK.im: Keep Erbil-bound travel on advance-approval with avoidance of the Koya, Khabat and Balisan areas and a flight-disruption fallback via Türkiye, treat Baghdad as High with armoured movement only, and for Türkiye maintain normal operations with same-day monitoring of protest calls and flood-damaged infrastructure in Istanbul.

OUTLOOK.a: Over the next 90 days North Africa splits into a stable-but-securitised Maghreb (Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia) and two states where external and internal security pressures are building (Egypt, Libya). The Western Sahara file peaks around the 31 October MINURSO renewal and the Algiers–Rabat sabotage-network case, likely producing rhetoric and small demonstrations rather than violence; Tunisia's opposition has shown it can again fill central Tunis, raising the frequency of protest-day disruption without, so far, violence. Egypt is edging toward a defensive military role against the Houthis (vote 26 October) and has escalated a lethal sovereignty campaign on the Sudan border, both of which keep Red Sea/Suez logistics and the southern frontier exposed. Libya's political track is unusually convergent (HoR leadership change, Türkiye deal, UN-brokered agreement) but security on the ground remains militia-driven, with recurring deadly ordnance incidents, oil-infrastructure interference and abductions.
dr: Egypt's parliamentary decision on 26 October on military support to Saudi Arabia, Houthi retaliation threats and the state of Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb shipping
UN Security Council votes on MINURSO (31 Oct) and UNSMIL (31 Oct), and the Algiers–Rabat confrontation over the Oran 'sabotage network' case
Economic grievance cycles in Tunisia (utility cuts, shortages, arrests of critics) and Morocco (youth unemployment, Ceuta migration pressure) that can mobilise crowds at short notice
ind: Egyptian parliament vote outcome and any announced deployment, followed by Houthi statements or attacks naming Egyptian or Suez-linked targets
Renewed armed clashes or drone strikes in Zawiya/western coastal corridor, Tripoli militia movements, or interference with the Sharara–Zawiya pipeline and Zawiya refinery
UGTT strike calls or repeat mass marches in Tunis; GenZ 212 or anti-normalisation calls in Morocco; any Polisario fire near Smara/Mahbes after the MINURSO vote
OUTLOOK.im: Maintain standard journey management for Morocco, Tunisia and Algeria's northern cities with protest-day avoidance of central Tunis and Rabat, and keep Algeria's southern/eastern borders and Egypt's North Sinai and Sudan frontier as no-go; build Red Sea/Suez contingency routing into Egypt itineraries ahead of the 26 October vote. Libya stays essential-only with armed escort, pre-cleared routes avoiding Zawiya and the western coastal road, and an air-evacuation plan.

OUTLOOK.a: Over the next 90 days the central Sahel will remain in sustained, multi-actor conflict with no credible path to de-escalation: JNIM retains the initiative around Bamako and in central Mali, ISSP is escalating in Ménaka and the Niger–Mali–Burkina tri-border, and all three juntas are leaning harder on Russian Africa Corps support and on indiscriminate air power that fuels reprisal cycles against civilians. In Nigeria the north-east insurgency has returned to overrunning bases and ambushing escorted convoys, and north-west banditry is now hitting military-escorted movements, while a confirmed Ebola case in Abuja introduces a health-security variable that could trigger screening, closures or travel restrictions if secondary transmission occurs. Niger's fuel crisis and post-mutiny purges raise the probability of a second coup attempt or urban unrest in Niamey, and the Arlit–Agadez attack shows the north is no longer insulated. Expect further mass-casualty attacks on security forces, continued JNIM–ISSP inter-factional fighting spilling across borders, and tightening operating space for any Western-linked organisation.
dr: JNIM–ISSP competition and the atrocity/reprisal cycle between jihadists, state forces, Africa Corps and allied militias (Ménaka, Tillabéri, Borno), which targets civilians seen as informants
Fuel and supply fragility: JNIM's blockade of Bamako's fuel routes and Niger's refinery/import shortfall, which degrade road movement, power and the state's own logistics
Weakening and fracturing state security forces: post-mutiny purges in Niger, Nigerian bases overrun and escorted convoys ambushed, growing dependence on drone strikes with high civilian tolls
ind: Any secondary Ebola transmission in Abuja or new imported cases in Lagos/Kano; airline or border screening measures announced by NCDC or neighbouring states
Attacks on or losses by Africa Corps units, or a second mutiny/coup attempt in Niamey or Bamako; further nationality-stripping decrees or arrests of senior officers
Successful JNIM/ISSP attacks on escorted fuel or passenger convoys into Bamako, Agadez or Maiduguri, or a renewed attack on a capital-city airport (Niamey, Bamako)
OUTLOOK.im: Mali and Niger should be held at no-go with all non-essential travel deferred and any residual presence covered by state-level clearance and air-only movement; Nigeria stays workable for Lagos and Abuja with armed, pre-cleared ground movement, but journey-management plans must now add Ebola screening, medical-evacuation cover and avoidance of Borno, Zamfara and the Abuja–Kaduna road.

OUTLOOK.a: Somalia: Wire-confirmed reporting shows the South West State conflict has widened to the point where Laftagareen-aligned forces hold every major Bay town except Baidoa, including Buur Hakaba on the Mogadishu road, with Ethiopian AU troops standing aside; the federally backed administration announced a counter-offensive on 18 October and Laftagareen on 20 October demanded President Mohamud step aside, so a fight for Baidoa itself is now the base case. In Mogadishu the electoral commission's unilateral April–May 2027 timetable has been rejected by the opposition, Puntland and Jubaland, keeping the June-style risk of armed political confrontation in the capital alive, while no large al-Shabaab attack in the city was wire-confirmed in the window. Rating 4 and rising trend are retained; posture remains no-go outside the airport/Halane enclave, with the Mogadishu–Baidoa road and all of Bay and Bakool regions closed. Over the next 90 days the Horn's three wars will remain unresolved and increasingly interlinked: Sudan's drone campaign has crossed into South Sudan's Abyei and is hitting power, dam and airport infrastructure in army-held areas, so Port Sudan, Khartoum and the Abyei-Kordofan belt stay no-go. In Ethiopia the federal counter-offensive has retaken Tigray's cities and installed a caretaker administration, but the TPLF is fighting on in the mountains, Fano holds much of rural Amhara and the Ethiopia-Eritrea confrontation is frozen rather than settled, with troops facing each other at Zalambessa and no diplomatic channel beyond US and UN pressure. Kenya is the regional hub but now carries a health-security overlay from the Ebola cluster and a US Level 3 advisory, while Djibouti's stability depends on events in Afar and Yemen rather than anything domestic. The most likely path is high-intensity attrition in Sudan, a contested but government-held Tigray, and a tense Ethiopia-Eritrea standoff that could tip into open border fighting within weeks on a single incident.
dr: Sudan's drone war expanding geographically (Abyei, Blue Nile, eastern dams, Khartoum airport) with mass-casualty strikes on civilian gatherings by both sides and no ceasefire track.

Ethiopia-Eritrea hostility: severed ties, troops on both sides of Zalambessa, Abiy's sea-access ambition and Eritrean denial of a documented incursion, with the TPLF and Fano insurgencies still active.
Red Sea/Yemen escalation: Houthi control of Perim and the Yemeni coast, refugee and migrant flows through Obock, and shipping disruption feeding fuel-price inflation and protest risk in Kenya.
ind: Any exchange of fire across the Eritrean border at Zalambessa, Rama or toward Assab, or Ethiopian armour moving north of the Mereb.
Further Sudanese strikes inside South Sudan or on the Abyei oil fields, and RSF drone hits on Port Sudan, Khartoum airport or the Merowe, Atbara or Setit dams.
Ebola cases in Kenya outside the known contact cluster, or a return of large-scale cost-of-living protests in Nairobi after the October fuel price rise.
OUTLOOK.im: Journey management should treat Sudan, South Sudan outside Juba and Ethiopia north of Addis as no-go, keep Eritrea on avoid, and run Addis, Djibouti and Nairobi as workable with advance planning, health screening for Ebola, and contingency routing for Djibouti corridor and Red Sea disruption.

OUTLOOK.a: Over the next 90 days the eastern Congo war is likely to intensify rather than settle: Kabila's assumption of the FRN leadership gives the Rwanda-backed insurgency a national political project and an explicit regime-change aim, Kinshasa has responded with a party ban and treason rhetoric, and the US-Qatar peace track has produced little change on the ground. Expect continued M23/FRN-FARDC-Wazalendo fighting with drones and artillery in Masisi, Lubero, Kalehe, Walungu and the Uvira highlands, persistent ADF and CODECO attacks on civilians in Ituri, and rising risk of politically driven arrests and unrest in Kinshasa. The record Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak (over 9,000 cases, 4,400 deaths, eight provinces, imported cases in Kenya) will keep straining access and health infrastructure in the east and could trigger border and travel restrictions.
dr: Kabila-led FRN consolidating M23/AFC and allied militias under an explicit aim to remove Tshisekedi by force, hardening both sides against the Washington/Doha peace track

Fragmented eastern battlefield (FARDC, Burundian troops, Wazalendo, foreign contractors vs M23/FRN, Twirwaneho; ADF and CODECO in Ituri) with drones and artillery and no effective ceasefire monitoring
Shrinking political space in Kinshasa (party bans, treason prosecutions, constitutional-change dispute) and Ebola/cholera emergencies that absorb state capacity and disrupt humanitarian access
ind: FRN/M23 offensive movement toward Walikale, Lubero/Butembo, Uvira or the Kalehe-Bukavu axis, or new drone strikes on FARDC airfields
Arrests of opposition figures, protests or security-force deployments in Kinshasa, and the content of Tshisekedi's planned address to the nation
Ebola case trajectory, new provinces or countries affected, and any border closures or flight restrictions by neighbours
OUTLOOK.im: Maintain no-go status for North/South Kivu and Ituri and treat Kinshasa as workable only with vetted drivers, advance planning and a political-unrest contingency; build Ebola screening, medevac and border-closure scenarios into every DRC journey plan.

OUTLOOK.a: The 90-day picture is driven by three political calendars. Brazil's 25 October runoff will be decided within days; either outcome leaves Rio's armed-group territorial control and lethal policing unchanged, and a Bolsonaro win would deepen US-Brazil security entanglement (CV/PCC terrorist designations, consular-security disputes) while a contested result could bring street mobilisation. Colombia's de la Espriella government has ended 'total peace', ordered four bombing raids since August and cancelled talks, so FARC-dissident and ELN retaliation on the Pan-American corridor, Catatumbo and Arauca will persist or intensify through year-end, with drones, car bombs and attacks on toll and road infrastructure the pattern. Venezuela's US-managed transition is stable but brittle: sanctions relief and oil investment continue, yet no election date exists and the 22 October mobilisation tests whether the Rodríguez government will tolerate opposition street pressure.
dr: Brazil runoff (25 Oct) with security as the defining issue and federal troops in 15 Rio-area municipalities
Colombian state offensive (air strikes, cancelled talks) and armed-group reprisals on the Pan-American Highway, Catatumbo and Arauca
Venezuela's unscheduled election, Machado's blocked return and opposition-chavista rival marches
ind: Post-runoff contestation or violence in Brazil; TSE/Defence Ministry troop deployment and any further lethal police incidents on Rio arteries
Further car bombs or drone strikes on Cauca/Nariño highways and toll plazas; ELN 'armed strike' declarations; attacks spreading to Cali or Bogotá
Conduct of the 22 October marches in Caracas (arrests, crowd control, clashes) and whether the Caracas talks produce an electoral calendar
OUTLOOK.im: Journey management should treat Rio as elevated through election week with route planning away from Avenida Brasil and favela-adjacent corridors, keep Colombian itineraries to air travel between major cities with no road moves south of Cali or into Norte de Santander/Arauca, and hold Caracas movements on the afternoon of 22 October pending reporting on the rival marches.

AAIA.s: On a Sunday afternoon a suicide car bomb was driven into the gate of the Elite Hotel on Lido Beach, a popular weekend venue for Mogadishu's politicians and business community, and a small team of gunmen then stormed the building. Security forces fought room to room for roughly seven hours before the last attacker was killed. The UN later put the toll at at least 17 dead. The attack re-established the Al-Shabaab 'gate VBIED then assault team' template against soft, high-status venues that would recur through 2024.

AAIA.tg: Hotel near AAIA used by officials and officers
AAIA.s: A car bomb detonated at the entrance of Hotel Afrik, on the main road between the city and the airport, and four gunmen fought their way inside. The siege lasted several hours; among the dead was a retired Somali general. Civilians trapped in the hotel were rescued by security forces, and the UN Special Representative condemned the attack the next day. The venue's location — on the airport approach and within sight of the Halane access route — made it the closest hotel-siege to AAIA in the period.

AAIA.tg: Civilians and soldiers at a checkpoint
AAIA.s: A suicide bomber wearing an explosive vest walked into a corrugated-tin teashop beside a government security checkpoint in Wadajir, the district that physically borders both the airport and the AU mission headquarters, and detonated among off-duty soldiers and civilians. At least 11 people were killed. Al-Shabaab claimed the attack; the prime minister condemned it as a 'barbaric act'. It illustrates the group's use of low-cost person-borne devices against checkpoint clusters on the airport's landward side.

AAIA.tg: AU convoy (claimed); school and civilians hit
AAIA.s: At 07:30 a suicide bomber in an SUV detonated beside a passing convoy on a busy Hodan road just as pupils were arriving at the neighbouring Mocaasir Primary and Secondary School. Al-Shabaab said the target was an AU Mission convoy; the blast instead killed eight people and injured 17, including teachers and children, and heavily damaged the school. The incident is a reminder that convoy-targeted VBIEDs on the KM4–airport axis produce heavy collateral casualties in the dense districts between the city centre and AAIA.

A suicide car bomber rammed a convoy on the main road leading to the AAIA/Halane entrance, killing around eight people. Al-Shabaab claimed the attack and said it targeted a convoy carrying Western contractors and security staff. The strike demonstrated the vulnerability of the single approach road that all airport and Halane traffic must use, and prompted a tightening of convoy procedures for the compound.

Gunmen penetrated the eastern area of Aden Adde International Airport and attacked a military position inside the perimeter; black smoke was visible near the runway during the firefight. Five people, including an AMISOM soldier, were killed before the two attackers were shot. The assault was coordinated with twin suicide bombings in Beledweyne the same day that killed dozens, including a federal MP. It remains the only confirmed ground penetration of the AAIA perimeter in the period and exposed gaps on the airfield's eastern (beach-side) edge.

AAIA.tg: Hotel used by officials and businessmen
AAIA.s: Two car bombs breached the Hayat Hotel's defences on a Friday evening and a team of gunmen barricaded themselves inside with hostages. Security forces took around 30 hours to clear the building floor by floor; 21 people were killed and over 100 injured, many by the second blast that hit responders and bystanders. It was the first major Mogadishu attack after President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's 2022 election and triggered his declaration of 'total war' on Al-Shabaab.
AAIA.src: Widely reported; 30-hour siege referenced at thedefensepost.com/2025/04/06

AAIA.s: At around 14:00 a vehicle bomb exploded at the Zobe junction outside the Ministry of Education; minutes later a second VBIED detonated as ambulances and crowds converged, destroying at least one ambulance. More than 120 people were killed and over 300 injured — the deadliest attack in Somalia since the October 2017 truck bomb at the same junction. Al-Shabaab admitted responsibility on 1 November, framing the ministry as a legitimate target. The sequenced 'second blast on first responders' tactic is the defining feature of this event.

AAIA.loc: Villa Rose Hotel, Bondhere (near Villa Somalia)
AAIA.tg: Hotel frequented by ministers and MPs
AAIA.s: Gunmen stormed the Villa Rose Hotel, a short walk from the presidential palace and a known residence for ministers, after a car bomb at the gate. The siege lasted roughly 20 hours; around nine people were killed and the environment minister was among the wounded. The attack showed Al-Shabaab's willingness to strike inside the government district despite the heightened security that followed the October Zobe bombing.

A bomb exploded in the Pearl Beach hotel restaurant on a Friday evening and seven gunmen then entered the building, taking diners hostage. Security forces freed 84 people during an overnight operation and killed all seven attackers; six civilians and three soldiers died. The attack repeated the 2020 Elite Hotel pattern on the same stretch of Lido Beach, underlining that beachfront leisure venues 4–5 km from AAIA remain a preferred soft target.

Several mortar rounds were fired into the airport complex, one of which killed a Ugandan soldier of the UN Guard Unit. It was the first lethal indirect-fire attack on AAIA in the 2024–25 series and marked a shift from ground assaults to stand-off IDF against the airport and Halane.

An attacker in military uniform opened fire on a group of Emirati and Bahraini trainers at the General Gordon base, killing four UAE soldiers and a Bahraini officer. Al-Shabaab claimed the attack. The incident highlighted the insider-threat risk at training sites and led to a review of vetting for foreign-supported units.

A suicide bomber blew himself up at the gate of the SYL Hotel, adjacent to the presidential palace, and five or six gunmen stormed inside. The siege ran for about 13 hours; three guards, two security officers and three soldiers were killed along with all the attackers, and 27 people were injured. The hotel had been attacked twice before, and the operation showed that even the palace perimeter zone could be penetrated by a small assault team.

Al-Shabaab detainees in Mogadishu Central Prison seized weapons, threw grenades and attempted a mass breakout. Custodial Corps and army reinforcements contained the attempt after a gunfight that left five prisoners and three soldiers dead and 21 injured. The government said no one escaped; Al-Shabaab claimed hundreds freed. The incident pointed to weapons and communications reaching detainees inside the capital's main prison.

A suicide car bomb exploded outside a café near the Daljirka Daahsoon monument where crowds had gathered to watch the Euro 2024 final. Reports of the toll range from five to more than nine killed, with about 20 injured. The attack, a day after the prison breakout attempt, targeted a predictable civilian gathering and showed the group's attention to timing against televised events.

On a Friday evening a suicide bomber detonated at the Beach View hotel and gunmen then opened fire on beach-goers and diners along Lido Beach. Thirty-seven civilians and a soldier were killed before the six attackers were shot — the deadliest attack in the capital in 2024 and the third major assault on the Lido strip since 2020. Lido's open beachfront and crowd density make it the hardest soft target in the city to protect.

An IED concealed inside a crowded tea shop in Daynile detonated mid-afternoon, killing at least 20 people, several of them security personnel who frequented the venue. The attack came two weeks after Lido Beach and showed Al-Shabaab's reach into the north-western districts along the Afgooye corridor — the same Daynile checkpoints that produce the bulk of Mogadishu's grenade and IED events in 2026.

A suicide car bomber attacked a NISA checkpoint on the Afgooye highway, the main western entry to the city, killing ten people including seven intelligence officers. Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility. The Afgooye corridor is the primary route by which VBIEDs are assembled in Lower Shabelle and moved toward the capital, and checkpoints on it are repeatedly targeted.

Six mortar rounds landed across the airport and the Halane compound, injuring several people and damaging residences used by ATMIS personnel and diplomats. No group claimed it. It was the second barrage of 2024 and showed the attackers' ability to range both the airfield and the diplomatic enclave from firing points in the city's southern districts.

Mortar rounds struck inside Halane, killing three people and injuring several; ATMIS condemned it as a 'deadly mortar attack'. This was the most lethal of the 2024 barrages and prompted additional counter-IDF measures around the compound's southern and western approaches.

AAIA.loc: Ceelgaabta, presidential motorcade route to airport
AAIA.s: A roadside bomb detonated beside the presidential motorcade at Ceelgaabta as it travelled from Villa Somalia toward the airport. The president was unhurt but reports put the dead at between four and a dozen, including a journalist. Al-Shabaab claimed the attack, which coincided with its spring offensive in Middle and Lower Shabelle and the loss of several towns to the group. It was the closest Al-Shabaab has come to the head of state in the period.

A day after the motorcade bombing, mortar rounds hit the area of the airport where UN personnel board aircraft and landed inside Halane near the Movcon area, just as Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed was arriving. Airport sirens sounded and flights were held; no casualties were reported. The timing against a VIP arrival is the clearest example of Al-Shabaab using IDF for political signalling rather than casualties.

AAIA.loc: AAIA open area, Halane, Kaawo Godey
AAIA.s: Around 06:05 six mortar rounds fell on open ground inside the airport, on Halane and on the Kaawo Godey residential area outside the fence, injuring a woman and a young man. A Turkish Airlines flight diverted to Djibouti and EgyptAir cancelled its service for the day. AUSSOM reported no casualties among its troops. The barrage followed a mortar attack on Warta Nabada and Boondheere the previous day, part of a sustained spring IDF campaign.

At least five mortar shells landed inside the Halane perimeter early on a Monday morning; it was not immediately clear whether anyone was hurt or which installations were hit. It was the third strike on the compound in roughly six weeks and reinforced the assessment that Al-Shabaab could fire on Halane at will from the southern districts.

A bomber dressed in military uniform joined a queue of young recruits at the Damaanyo base gate and detonated a vest at about 09:20, killing 15 recruits and five civilians and injuring 15. Al-Shabaab claimed the attack with inflated casualty figures. The event showed the continued ability to place a person-borne device at a predictable, crowded military access point in Hodan, roughly 3.5 km from AAIA.

At least six mortar rounds hit Halane and properties near the airport two days after the Damaanyo bombing; emergency sirens sounded along the airport perimeter and Al-Shabaab claimed the attack within hours. Somali Guardian counted it as the fourth attack on the base in recent weeks. Damage was limited to property, but the cadence (four barrages in nine weeks) is the densest IDF campaign against AAIA/Halane in the period.

A suicide bomber reached the morning roll-call at the Jaalle Siyaad academy, headquarters of the 14th October Brigade, and detonated among officers; gunfire followed. Four SNA officers were killed and several injured. Six senior officers were detained over the security breach and the ministry restricted reporting. Coming two years after a deadlier 2023 bombing at the same academy, it underlined persistent insider and access-control weaknesses at Hodan military sites.

AAIA.loc: Godka Jilow prison, near Villa Somalia
AAIA.t: VBIED + armed assault in NISA-style vehicles/uniforms
AAIA.s: A car bomb breached the entrance of the Godka Jilow underground prison near the presidential palace and a seven-man team in military-style uniforms, driving vehicles painted to resemble NISA's, attempted to free detained fighters. The siege lasted about six hours before all seven attackers were killed; the government said no prisoners escaped and did not publish its own losses. The attack came hours after the city reopened dozens of roads and is the most recent confirmed complex assault by Al-Shabaab in the capital.

AAIA.t: Political violence: government shelling/assault on opposition compounds
AAIA.tg: Residences of ex-PM Khaire and ex-President Sharif
AAIA.s: Over two days government forces shelled and assaulted the Barmuudo compound of former PM Hassan Ali Khaire and then the Marinayo residence of former President Sharif Sheikh Ahmed, after the collapse of election talks and the expiry of the presidential mandate. NISA chief Mahad Salad negotiated Khaire's withdrawal and escorted him back to his residence inside the AAIA perimeter, where opposition leaders had been based before dispersing to clan areas. Western ambassadors, speaking from Halane, pressed for a halt. Casualty figures were never verified. Not an Al-Shabaab event, but the clearest case of Mogadishu's political conflict reaching the airport perimeter.

Defence Minister Ahmed Moalim Fiqi said authorities had removed 260 armed men from opposition leaders' residences in Mogadishu, alleging the UAE had armed the opposition and that Puntland- and Jubaland-linked forces had been brought into the city. He denied any plan to arrest opposition leaders. Only the government's account is available. The operation is the precursor indicator for a repeat of the June clashes.

AAIA.loc: Hormuud HQ, Bakara Market & airport road
AAIA.s: Police entered Hormuud's headquarters in Bakara Market and its main management office on the road to the airport under a court warrant, reportedly in connection with the Southwest State fighting. No violence was reported. The relevance for AAIA is the use of the airport road for a politically charged security operation and the risk of escalation involving Somalia's largest private company.
